https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/benchling/33b3d.description:
Biotechnology is rewriting life as we know it, from the medicines we take, to the crops we grow, the materials we wear, and the household goods that we rely on every day. But moving at the new speed of science requires better technology.

Benchling’s mission is to unlock the power of biotechnology. The world’s most innovative biotech companies use Benchling’s R&D Cloud to power the development of breakthrough products and accelerate time to milestone and market.

Come help us bring modern software to modern science.


ROLE OVERVIEW

Benchling is building a world-class Professional Services team to drive implementations for our rapidly expanding customer base. Implementation Managers work with our customers, from small Biotech startups to the largest BioPharmas in the world to develop a deep understanding of their R&D Processes, and roll out solutions that transform how their research teams work together.


To be successful in this role, you will leverage your scientific background, project management skills, and product expertise to drive successful implementations of the Benchling platform. You will work hand in hand with the research scientists at our customers, and teams throughout Benchling to implement our solutions, and ensure our customers are successful. Implementation Managers lead all aspects of customer rollouts from requirements analysis and solution design, to configurations, testing, training, and onboarding users onto the system. In addition, you have fluent or native proficiency in French and have experience working with French speaking customers.

 


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Manage initial rollouts for new Benchling customers as well as expansion projects with new teams or for new processes at existing customers

 - Own implementation success from project kickoff to go-live, leveraging strong project management skills, scientific expertise, and deep product knowledge.

 - Build and execute detailed project plans, own project activities, work with other team members to execute on project deliverables to ensure on time, on budget, high quality deployments.

 - Understand customers' scientific workflows and determine how Benchling can best be leveraged to meet their key business needs.

 - Lead requirements and design workshops, perform data modeling & application configuration, develop test plans and guide UAT execution, train and onboard users.

 - Act as a trusted advisor for customers, guiding them through the implementation ensuring they leverage and apply Benchling Best Practices.

 - Understand and document customer pain points, advocate for them internally to influence product changes.

 - Identify and work with sales on opportunities for account expansion post go-live. 


QUALIFICATIONS

 - MS or Ph.D. in Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Immunology, Bioinformatics, Biological Engineering or a related field.

 - At least 2 years of experience in a lab or R&D setting, ideally in antibody discovery or strain engineering or process development. You must be able to empathize with scientists and quickly understand complicated scientific concepts.

 - Software Implementation experience, preferably with a SaaS software company.

 - Strong communication skills. You must be able to quickly and effectively connect with a range of stakeholders, including scientists, IT project leads, and executives.

 - Self-starter with the ability to be successful in a startup environment.

 - Curious, creative, and tenacious. You should be excited to collaborate with customers and other Benchling teammates as a thought partner.

 - Ability to travel up to 25% based on customer and project needs.

 - Fluent or native proficiency in French

 - Experience using Benchling, especially if you’ve been a Benchling administrator, is preferred but not required.

 


HOW WE WORK

We offer a flexible hybrid work arrangement that prioritizes in-office collaboration. Employees are expected to be on-site 3 days per week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday).


HOW WE WORK

Flexible Hybrid Work: We offer a flexible hybrid work arrangement that prioritizes in-office collaboration. Employees are expected to be on-site 3 days per week.


SALARY RANGE

Benchling takes a market-based approach to pay. The candidate's starting pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, interview performance, and work location.

Total Compensation includes the following:

 - Competitive total rewards package

 - Fertility healthcare and family-forming benefits

 - Four months of fully paid parental leave

 - Home office stipend

 - Mental health benefits + wellness stipend

 - Learning and development reimbursement

 - 25 days vacation days + public holidays

 - Company-wide Winter holiday shutdown

 - Sabbaticals for 5-year and 10-year anniversaries

 - Remote perks including travel to hubs

 - In-office perks (Zurich Only - In Office)

 - Commuter benefits (Zurich Only - In Office)

#LI-Hybrid

#BI-Hybrid

Benchling welcomes everyone.

We believe diversity enriches our team so we hire people with a wide range of identities, backgrounds, and experiences.

We are an equal opportunity employer. That means we don’t discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We also consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law, including but not limited to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

https://apply.workable.com/debiopharm/j/.description:
Join us at the cutting edge of oncology innovation. In this role, you will immerse yourself in the exciting and innovative field of liquid-biopsy based biomarker investigation in oncology with direct application to our internal project’s portfolio.  
Liquid biopsies represent a major advance in the molecular diagnostic space and are increasingly used in clinical trials. By replacing invasive tissue biopsies with minimally invasive blood sampling, They facilitate patient recruitment, enable earlier assessment of treatment response, and improve  identification of appropriate patient populations. In addition, they provide valuable insight into disease biology  and support the development of predictive and prognostic biomarkers. Debiopharm is now expanding the implementation of these technologies across our portfolio.  
As an intern in the Personalised Medicine team, part of the Translation Medicine Team, you will participate in fore-front clinical investigations, contribute directly to patient-centric clinical trials design and help shape the future of targeted oncology therapies. 
Working under the guidance and mentorship of an Associate Principal Scientist, your core responsibilities will be but not limited to: 
perform advanced data analyses on liquid biopsy sequencing results and propose additional investigations 
drive the integration of liquid biopsy approaches within the context of our portfolio, provide input into the clinical trial protocols 
support internal advocacy for the adoption of liquid biopsy technologies within project teams and management 
support the definition and implementation of biomarker strategies where liquid biopsy data are critical 

Your profile 
 
PhD in Life sciences, molecular biology, genetics, or a related discipline 
Experience in large datasets analysis 
Comfortable with using basic bioinformatic tools  
Previous experience with molecular diagnostic assays is an asset 
Ready to work in cross-functional team and fast-paced environment 
A collaborative spirit, looking to tackle new challenges  
Excellent communication skills in English (oral and written) 
What we Offer: 
Being part of a company where innovation, collaboration, and impact aren’t just values — they’re how we work every day 
Partner with teams across disciplines, at the forefront of oncology and anti-infective development 
An inclusive and respectful workplace — proud to be Equal-Pay certified 
Grow in a culture that values people, purpose, and performance 
A chance to grow, share, and shape the future of healthcare 
 
What to Expect in the Recruitment Process: 
If your application is selected, you’ll be invited to interviews with Talent Acquisition and the Hiring Manager via Teams, followed by a panel interview and reference checks. Communication is handled via Workable—check your spam folder for emails from *@outbound.workable.com. 
 
Please contact our HR Department prior to submitting any profiles. We cannot accept unsolicited applications from agencies or recruiters.

Labcorp is a global leader in laboratory services, providing the insights and answers that help healthcare providers, patients, researchers, pharmaceutical companies and health systems make confident decisions and improve outcomes. Through our unparalleled science, data, technology and laboratory network, we advance diagnostics, accelerate innovation and help address some of the world’s most important health challenges. As we shape the future of healthcare, we are leveraging advanced technologies, intelligent digital solutions and data-driven innovation across our operations to enhance how work gets done and deliver greater value to customers and patients. With our global scale and deep expertise, you’ll have the opportunity to do meaningful work, grow your career and make a real impact on people’s health around the world. Together, we’re improving health and improving lives.

Labcorp is seeking a Staff Scientist in Flow Cytometry for our site in Geneva, Switzerland.

Job Responsibilities
Perform complex troubleshooting and assist in leading initiatives to solve challenging scientific problems with assays or instrumentation.
Apply and interpret scientific theories, concepts, techniques and regulatory requirements in clinical studies and accept leadership role in developing scientific approaches.
Provide consultation to scientific and operational staff on technical issues.
Respond to unscheduled deadlines, client needs, crises, etc. without neglecting other duties.
Assist with regular monitoring and evaluation of clinical assays to ensure effective scientific performance.
Provide technical training for operational staff.
Provide technical/scientific consultation to departments outside the lab (i.e., Project Management) as requested.
Contribute to long-term planning and technical policies of the department.
Assist in managing scientific vendor relationships to troubleshoot issues and improve capabilities.
Participate in client visits.
Regularly read literature related to scientific area of expertise to remain current in knowledge.
Give presentations to clients and professional groups.
Attend meetings, conferences, symposia, and seminars to promote CLS’s capabilities within dedicated scientific area.

Minimum Qualifications

PhD in science

4 or more years of experience in Spectral Flow Cytometry using Cytek Aurora instrumentation.

Preferred Qualifications

3 or more years of experience in clinical laboratory automation, system software, Microsoft applications and laboratory statistics.

Additional Job Standards
Highly skilled in conducting research, data interpretation, and writing reports.
Proven track record of method development.
Experience performing scientific presentations and preparing scientific publications.
Good team player with effective communication skills with technical staff, business development staff, peers and clients.
Attention to detail and interpretation of scientific data.
Demonstrated problem prevention, detection and resolution.
Fluent in English, French is considered as a plus.

If you are looking for a company where you can gain exposure to a wide variety of science and explore a multitude of career paths across the drug development spectrum, consider working at Labcorp as a Staff Scientist in Flow Cytometry.
In this role, you will participate in scientific activities and initiatives in support of global Laboratory Operations. You will perform complex trouble-shooting and problem-solving, supporting Lab Operations to ensure smooth transition of assays into production. You will participate in developing/identifying new strategies, techniques and instrumentation for the development of new ventures in the scientific area of expertise for Central Laboratory Services global Laboratory Operations.

Support the Director of Market Access to develop and execute market access strategies that enable optimal launch, pricing, reimbursement, and sustainable access to a specialty care indications across international markets and designated partner regions. The role requires strategic thinking, cross-functional collaboration, and solid knowledge of international market access policies, health economics, and stakeholder engagement to deliver timely and equitable patient access.
Main responsibilities
Planning: Support development and implementation of comprehensive market access strategies tailored to launching Specialty care product, diverse international markets and partner regions, aligned with corporate objectives, regulatory landscapes, and local affiliate needs.
Pricing and reimbursement: Collaborate to secure pricing, reimbursement, and formulary inclusion for new and existing products, leveraging health economic models, budget impact analyses, and value-based arguments.

By joining Bio-Techne, you’ll join a company with a powerful and positive purpose of enabling cutting-edge research in Life Sciences and Clinical Diagnostics. Bio-Techne, and all of its brands, provides tools for researchers to further treat and prevent disease worldwide.

Pay Range: CHF76,900 - CHF123,100
Placement within the salary range will vary depending on experience, qualifications, geographic location, and internal equity considerations.

Type of contract: 12 months fixed term contact

Job Description
Are you a scientist, passionate about new technologies, looking for an exciting challenge where you can have an impact on the future growth of your company? We are looking for an ‘Application Development Scientist’ to work in the Application Development team researching and testing new solutions for spatial multi-omics assays on tissue samples using Bio-Techne Spatial instruments.

Your Missions

Test, optimize, and validate new markers for immunofluorescent multiplex stainings on tissue samples

Investigate novel & innovative solutions for spatial-omics assays on Bio-Techne Spatial microfluidic platforms

Develop a fine understanding of in situ protein and RNA detection methodologies

Acquire images, process them, analyze data, and report results concisely

Explore and understand the biological background of the target markers under development

Contribute to the continuous development of devices and software

Interact with multidisciplinary team of hardware and software engineers and researchers

This position reports to the Application Development Manager

Qualifications
Your ideal profile

Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. 

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.


ABOUT THE ROLE

This is not a lab technician position. This is a senior scientist who owns assay quality, data QC and controls, and production troubleshooting across the entire experimental pipeline.

The production team runs 150+ experiments per month across expression, BLI, SPR, thermostability, and enzyme activity. When something goes wrong (failed expression, anomalous binding data, instrument artifacts), this person diagnoses the root cause and fixes it. As the assay and instrumentation portfolio expands, this person translates new R&D methods into production-ready protocols, builds robust methods that junior technicians can execute reliably, and designs comprehensive controls that enable automated QC and data processing.

This is a player-coach position. You will still run experiments personally, especially as you integrate into the lab, but you will also elevate the whole team's capabilities.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Troubleshoot production failures across the full pipeline. A batch of proteins isn't expressing: is it the construct design, the expression system, or the media? BLI sensorgrams look noisy: is it the sensor tips, the sample prep, or an instrument issue? You figure it out, fix it, and make the cause easier to identify next time.

 - Develop and document SOPs for new assays as the portfolio expands. Take methods from the R&D team and make them production-ready: robust, reproducible, and executable by junior technicians without hand-holding.

 - Mentor a growing production team. Set quality standards, review data, train new hires, and build a culture where people flag problems early instead of hiding them.

 - Work at the intersection of biology, automation, and QC. Collaborate with researchers, laboratory technicians, and automation engineers on protocol optimization for work cells, and with software on LabOS protocol integration.

 - Own the relationship between assay science and throughput. The easy version of every assay doesn't scale, and the scalable version often sacrifices quality. You find the right tradeoff.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Deep hands-on expertise in protein production: expression (E. coli, mammalian, cell-free), purification (IMAC, SEC), and biophysical characterization (BLI and SPR at minimum). This isn't negotiable. You need to have done this work yourself, at volume.

 - PhD in protein biochemistry, biophysics, or a relevant field, plus 3–5 years in a production or development role at a CRO, foundry, or high-throughput lab. Academic postdocs count if the work was high-throughput and production-oriented.

 - Experience with high-throughput workflows. You're comfortable with 96-well plates and liquid handlers, not just single-column purifications. You've optimized protocols for scale, not just for one perfect result.

 - Mentorship mindset. You've managed or trained junior scientists before. You enjoy teaching and get satisfaction from watching your team grow.

 - Troubleshooting instinct. When data looks wrong, your first impulse is to understand why, not to rerun the experiment and hope it works.

 - Quality-obsessed but pragmatic. You care deeply about data quality, but you also understand that production has deadlines and sometimes "good enough" is the right call.

 - Bridge between R&D and production. You can speak both languages: the exploratory mindset of research and the reproducibility demands of production.


DETAILS

 - Location: Lausanne, Switzerland (on-site)

 - Type: Full time

 - Start date: ASAP



Application deadline

We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/adaptyv/8845165.description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. 

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Our lab produces binding data faster than any one person can look at it. Runs come off the Gators and the Carterra, go through our processing pipeline, and land in a review queue. Somebody with real judgment then has to decide: is this curve real? Is that a fit artifact or a genuine two-state binding event? Does this replicate get delivered, or does the sample get re-run? That person is you.

The second half of the job is talking to the customer about it. When a design team gets a plate back and three of their best predictions look like non-binders, they want to talk to someone who can explain why: reference subtraction, avidity, an off-rate at the edge of what the instrument resolves, or simply a bad protein. You'll be that person, on the call, sharing your screen, walking through sensorgrams.

This is a role for a scientist who is very good at kinetics and also likes people. If you like one but not the other, you'll be unhappy here.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Review the binding data coming out of the lab. Every SPR and BLI run passes through our processing pipeline and then to human review, and you're the expert eye on the output. You decide what gets delivered, what gets flagged, and what gets re-run.

 - Judge the curves, not just the numbers. A clean-looking Kd on a bad fit is worse than no number at all. You know the difference between a real off-rate and a drifting baseline, and you can say why.

 - Review data from our other assays too: thermostability, expression, developability, enzyme activity. Binding is the core of the role but it isn't all of it.

 - Talk to customers about their results. Deliverable walkthroughs, follow-up questions, and the awkward conversation when the data doesn't say what they hoped. You explain what we measured, how confident we are, and what to do next.

 - Turn review into experimental design. When something needs a re-run, you decide what changes: orientation, regeneration, concentration series, or a switch from BLI to SPR for the sensitivity.

 - Analyze at the batch level, not just the sample level. With hundreds of results per experiment, you should be writing a script to find the pattern rather than clicking through a queue. Systematic drift, a bad reference channel, or a target lot behaving differently than the last one shows up in aggregate long before it shows up in any single curve.

 - Feed what you learn back into the pipeline. When you catch a case where automation passed something it shouldn't have, or failed something it shouldn't have, that becomes a concrete requirement for the software team.

 - Work closely with production (what actually happened in the lab), QC (systematic quality), and customer success (the relationship around the science).


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - MSc / PhD in biochemistry, biophysics, or a relevant field, plus 3+ years working hands-on with binding kinetics.

 - Deep SPR and BLI experience. Biacore, Carterra, Octet, Gator: the platform matters less than the fact that you've run these assays, troubleshot them, and interpreted a lot of data from them. You've seen enough sensorgrams to know immediately when one is lying to you.

 - Real fitting judgment. 1:1 vs. bivalent, when steady-state is appropriate and when it isn't, how mass transport and avidity distort a result. You can defend a Kd, or refuse to report one.

 - Strong data analysis skills. Python or R, enough to pull a few hundred results out of a database, fit them, plot them, and find the outliers. This role generates too much data to review by hand.

 - You use AI tools seriously. We run on Claude Code and similar tooling internally, and the people who get the most done here are the ones who reach for it by default: writing the analysis script, querying the database, building the one-off dashboard. You don't need to have done this before, but you need to want to. If your instinct is that real scientists do it by hand, this isn't the place.

 - A self-starter who works independently. Nobody is going to hand you a prioritized queue every morning. You'll figure out what matters most, go do it, and tell us what you found.

 - A fast learner. Our platform, our assays, and our software change constantly. You'll be handed unfamiliar tools and expected to be productive with them quickly.

 - Startup speed, not academic pace. Experiments ship to paying customers on deadlines. Getting a good answer this week beats a perfect one next quarter, and we'd rather flag an ambiguous result than sit on it.

 - Comfortable in front of customers. Many are PhD-level scientists at pharma companies and AI labs, and they will push back. You should enjoy that conversation rather than dread it.

 - Able to explain hard things simply. Some customers are biophysicists. Some are ML researchers who have never touched a pipette. You adjust without condescending to either.

 - Honest about uncertainty. When the data is ambiguous, you say so, to us and to the customer. We would much rather flag a weak result than ship a confident wrong one.

 - Familiarity with other biophysical or functional assays (DSF, HPLC, plate-based activity assays) is a plus.


DETAILS

 - Location: Lausanne, Switzerland (on-site)

 - Type: Full time

 - Start date: ASAP



Application deadline

We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

 - Work with the software and ML teams to specify, review, and improve the automated data pipelines that process instrument outputs, feeding back precise requirements for what to flag, auto-reject, or route to human review.

 - Connect experimental results back to the protein side — sequence, structure, and design — so wet-lab data and computational models reinforce each other.

 - Turn foundry output into structured, documented, benchmark-grade datasets that are a genuine asset for our customers and for training and evaluating protein-design models.

 - Apply real statistical rigor to multi-condition data at scale — thousands of samples across hundreds of simultaneous experiments — and make the results interpretable and comparable across runs.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Strong data science / bioinformatics background — you're fluent in Python (pandas, numpy, the scientific stack) and comfortable owning messy, real-world experimental data end to end.

 - Genuine biology grounding — you understand proteins, assays, and sequence/structure/function well enough to know what the data means, not just how to process it. You don't need to be a bench scientist, but you can't be biology-blind.

 - Statistical maturity — process control, anomaly detection, handling variability and batch effects; you can tell drift from noise and defend the call.

 - Prolific builder with the receipts to prove it. You've shipped a lot — pipelines, tools, models, datasets — and can point to concrete things you built end to end and put into real use, not prototypes that died in a notebook. You move fast, systematize what works, and have no patience for babysitting a fixed dashboard.

 - AI-native builder. It's 2026 — you build with coding agents like Claude Code as a default, and you have sharp judgment about what they produce.

 - Interdisciplinary by instinct. You're energized working across the lab bench, software, and ML, and you treat automation and data infrastructure as part of your job.

 - Bonus: experience with protein/sequence-structure data (bioinformatics tooling, structural data), ML on experimental data, or building datasets for model training and benchmarking.


DETAILS

 - Location: Lausanne, Switzerland (on-site)

 - Type: Full time

 - Start date: ASAP



Application deadline

We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

Who You Are

This includes assay development and validation, multicolour spectral panel design, and expertise in imaging flow cytometry, metabolic and functional assays.

The Position
The ML for Biosystems Engineering group led by Jonas Fleck at the Institute of Human Biology (IHB) in Basel, Switzerland is seeking a Postdoctoral Researcher to develop machine learning methods for organoid phenotyping and high-throughput screening. Join us to develop next-generation computational methods for drug discovery with complex human model systems.
 
The Opportunity

You will lead a research project developing computational methods to address important challenges in organoid engineering and drug discovery. Working in a highly collaborative environment with outstanding computational and experimental scientists, you'll develop state-of-the-art statistical and machine learning methods to tackle challenging questions in human biology and disease.
You'll have the chance to work with rich, high-content datasets from complex human model systems, such as large-scale perturbation experiments with multi-modal readouts. In collaboration with experimental scientists at IHB, you will also have the opportunity to shape future experiments, enabling you to develop methods with direct translational impact.
Possible research areas may include:
Causal inference and mechanism discovery from perturbation experiments
Predictive modeling and analysis for high-throughput screening
Computational methods for quantitative comparison of spatial, genomic, and other molecular profiles from organoid models with patient data.
Your work will connect computational innovation with experimental applications, contributing to the development of next-generation human model systems for drug discovery. You will publish your research, contribute open-source tools to the broader scientific community, and gain exposure to drug discovery and development while building your scientific independence as a computational researcher.

Who You are:

PhD in computational biology, computer science, machine learning, bioinformatics, or related technical fields.
Track record of conducting impactful independent research, demonstrated through publications, preprints, or substantial research software contributions.
Strong research experience in statistical or machine learning methods, ideally applied to genomics or other high-dimensional biological data.
Proficiency in Python and experience with modern ML and scientific computing frameworks such as JAX, PyTorch or TensorFlow.
Strong scientific programming and software engineering practices, including version control, testing, reproducible research workflows, and agentic development tools.
Creativity, scientific curiosity, and enthusiasm for developing computational methods that address challenging problems in biomedical research.
Ability and motivation to work closely with experimental scientists and contribute to collaborative, interdisciplinary projects.

Nice to have:
Experience applying machine learning to biomedical data, including genomics, imaging, spatial, or multimodal datasets.
Experience with perturbation experiments, causal inference, high-throughput screening, or predictive modeling.
Contributions to open-source software or scientific computing tools.
Experience working closely with experimental collaborators.

Technical details:

To be considered, your application needs a CV (including a list of relevant publications) and a cover letter describing your research interests.

About the Institute of Human Biology (IHB) & Basel:
The Institute of Human Biology (IHB) is a research center in Basel, Switzerland, dedicated to engineering advanced human model systems for drug discovery, development, and precision medicine. The IHB fosters an interdisciplinary environment bridging academic and pharmaceutical research, connecting biologists, engineers, and data scientists. It has close ties to Roche's Pharmaceutical Research and Early Development (pRED) organization and Genentech (gRED), and collaborates with leading academic institutions including ETH Zürich, University of Basel, and EPFL, as well as globally. Basel is an international hub for research and innovation, cultivating training environments through institutions like the University of Basel and ETH Zürich's Department of Biosystems Sciences and Engineering, creating a melting pot of research development and commercialization.

Job Description SummaryNovartis BioMedical Research (BR) is the innovation engine of Novartis that collaborates across the company and beyond, focusing on powerful new technologies that have the potential to help produce therapeutic breakthroughs for patients. Translational Medicine (TM) is the clinical research arm of Novartis BR, and includes about 900 associates globally. TM plays a pivotal role in bringing innovative medicines to patients, by building on research advances to develop new therapies, and bridging drug discovery and clinical application.
The TM Discovery & Profiling (TMDP) is a group of physicians and clinical researchers who drive innovative science from discovery to the patient through the selection, profiling, and effective development of medicines. Translational medicine experts oversee Phase 1 and 2 clinical trials to demonstrate proof-of-mechanism and proof-of-concept (PoC) in patients, as well as support for later Phase 3 development. Translational medicine experts are key and highly visible members of global cross-functional project teams that design and implement early research and discovery projects, that then culminate in clinical PoC studies. Translational medicine experts collaborate with colleagues in biology and chemistry to identify targets in diseases with significant unmet medical needs and provide input on likely clinical development pathways. The early clinical trials led by our translational medicine experts are among the most critical steps in drug development at Novartis. After PoC and if the program proceeds to full development, the translational medicine expert continues as a key member of the full development team up to and including registration.

You partner closely with experimental scientists, computational chemists, and machine learning teams across Roche's small-molecule research organisation to translate evolving scientific challenges into scalable computational solutions.

We are looking for a highly motivated data scientist with a strong enthusiasm for chemical biology and pushing the technology to the next step, who is interested in performing state-of-the-art research in the pharmaceutical industry.

Introduction
The CERN ATLAS Team plays a major role in the construction of the future silicon ATLAS Inner Tracker (ITk). In particular, the CERN Detector Technologies (DT) team focuses on the realisation of the Pixel Outer Barrel for the ITk. Our activities include the design, prototyping and assembly of the support structures and tooling as well as the final detector integration, installation and testing. As a mechanical/electromechanical technician in the CERN-DT Team, you will join the Engineering Office Section (EP-DT-EO) and work closely with personnel from the ATLAS Group (EP-ATL) and the Technical Coordination Team of the ATLAS Experiment in the design and construction of the ATLAS ITk Pixel Outer Barrel.
Functions
Participate in the production, testing and installation of the Pixel Outer System services and their support structures (e.g. trolleys).
Support the design, manufacturing and installation of temporary services and infrastructure for testing during the integration of the Pixel Detector.
Participate hands-on in the integration of the Pixel Outer System and its insertion into ITk in the SR1 cleanroom, contributing to the development and fabrication of the corresponding tooling.
Participate in the ITk installation in the ATLAS cavern, supporting preparation of Pixel services for installation as well as connections after insertion.
Document manufacturing and installation procedures as well QC information of tools and production parts to ensure traceability.

Introduction:
You will join the Technology Department's Machine Protection and Electrical Integrity (MPE) Group, which develops and maintains systems that protect accelerator equipment, including magnets and particle-beam-related installations.
Working in a collaborative team of software engineers, you will design, develop and maintain reliable software that supports the safe and efficient operation of the Large Hadron Collider and its injector complex. You will have the opportunity to solve challenging engineering problems, collaborate with experts across different disciplines and contribute to systems that are essential to CERN's scientific mission. 
Functions:
Design, implement, test and maintain software components that interface with equipment protection and interlock systems.
Monitor deployed applications, investigate technical issues and improve reliability, availability and maintainability.
Work with engineers, technical specialists and accelerator operations teams during commissioning, testing and operation.
Understand user requirements, contribute to technical decisions and help deliver sustainable software solutions.
Collaborate with colleagues to strengthen development workflows, automated testing, continuous integration and software quality, including exploring AI-assisted development tools where appropriate.
Provide technical guidance and mentoring to colleagues and students.

As a Mechanical Engineer for Vacuum you will join the team working on the vacuum systems for a future accelerator at CERN (FCC-ee) and contribute to the selection, characterisation and validation of materials and processes for ultra-high vacuum components. In this role, you will be involved in defining samples and prototypes, their production and procurement, as well as their testing and validation.
Your responsibilities
Actively participate in the development of the FCC-ee vacuum systems, particularly in materials and process selection, characterisation and validation, as well as prototyping.
Contribute to the internalisation and in-house development of key manufacturing technologies for large component production.
Collaborate with a dynamic team dedicated to the FCC-ee study.
Communicate regularly with CERN-wide services and external companies or institutes.
 
Your profile
Experience with metallic, in particular copper alloys, and ceramic materials for UHV applications.
Experience with metallic and ceramic additive manufacturing processes, including plasma spray, cold gas dynamic spray and 3D SLM printing.
Experience with metals hot and cold work processing and welding technologies. Experience with Laser and/or Friction Stir Welding is an advantage.
Skills
Fabrication of mechanical parts with CNC machine, in particular with CAM software.
Production of samples for materials characterisation including microscopic observations.
Prior knowledge or use of WorkNC is an advantage.
Design of mechanical parts with CAD program. Use of CATIA is an advantage.
Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the other language.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
You have a professional background in Mechanical/Materials & Process Engineering (or a related field) and have either:
a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;
or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

Join CERN's Polymer Laboratory within the Superconducting Magnet Technology section and contribute to the development and qualification of advanced polymer and composite materials.
In this role, you will take part in the design, validation and implementation of innovative materials for high-field superconducting magnets.
Your responsibilities:
Contribute to the development of novel polymer and composite materials for superconducting magnets, with particular emphasis on cryogenic operation, high-voltage insulation and radiation resistance.
Design and validate manufacturing and processing techniques for superconducting magnet insulation systems.
Contribute to the laboratory developments by identifying material technologies and processing techniques, as well as establishing new experimental capabilities.
Your profile:
Experience in material characterisation techniques, such as mechanical, thermal or chemical analyses.
Experience in composite and/or polymer processing techniques.
Knowledge of superconducting magnet construction and technologies, or of materials for cryogenic, high-voltage or radiation environments, would be an asset.
Skills:
Knowledge of materials science.
Knowledge and application of material testing.
Ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary teams.
Knowledge of cryogenics technology is a plus.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
You have a professional background in Material, Chemical, Mechanical Engineering (or a related field) and have either:
a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;
or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

En tant que cheffe ou chef de clinique titulaire d’un titre de spécialiste en pneumologie, vous assurez l’ensemble des activités cliniques du service et évoluez dans un environnement universitaire, à l’interface des soins, de l’enseignement et de la recherche. Grâce à un tournus trimestriel au sein des différentes unités spécialisées, vous développez une expertise diversifiée couvrant aussi bien la pratique hospitalière qu’ambulatoire en faisant preuve de polyvalence. Vous intervenez notamment dans la prise en charge des pneumopathies interstitielles, des complications pulmonaires chez les patientes ou patients immunodéprimés, de la transplantation pulmonaire, de la pneumologie interventionnelle ainsi que des troubles respiratoires du sommeil, en collaboration étroite avec le Centre de médecine du sommeil.
Vous rejoignez une équipe soudée composée de 9 chefs et cheffes de clinique, 4 médecins adjoints et adjointes et 5 médecins internes, sous la responsabilité de la professeure cheffe de service. Vous collaborez étroitement avec une équipe pluridisciplinaire regroupant infirmiers et infirmières spécialisées, techniciens et techniciennes en physiologie respiratoire, personnel administratif ainsi que les différents centres et départements médicaux de l’institution.
Vous assurez la prise en charge diagnostique et thérapeutique des pathologies respiratoires aiguës et chroniques. Vous participez à l’évaluation et au suivi de situations complexes, incluant notamment la dyspnée, la tuberculose, l’insuffisance respiratoire et les différents domaines médico-techniques de la spécialité.
Vous faites preuve de résilience, de sens clinique et d’une grande capacité d’analyse dans la prise en charge de situations parfois complexes. Grâce à votre sens de l’organisation et à votre capacité à prioriser, vous assurez efficacement vos activités cliniques tout en répondant aux multiples sollicitations (patients et patientes, téléphones, correspondances, réunions). Vous veillez à maintenir une communication claire, bienveillante et adaptée avec les patients et patientes, leurs proches ainsi qu’avec l’ensemble des professionnels impliqués dans leur prise en charge, en adaptant votre discours à leur compréhension.
En vous appuyant sur votre esprit d’équipe, vous faites preuve de solidarité face aux imprévus. En tant que cheffe ou chef de clinique, vous participez activement à la supervision et à la formation des médecins internes du département de médecine dans le domaine de la pneumologie, en adoptant une posture de mentorat et en partageant votre expertise.

What you'll do
You’ll take your first steps into the world of work at CERN — a place where learning and discovery go hand in hand. You’ll join a team of experts and contribute to real projects that connect science, technology and innovation. Every day will bring opportunities to learn new skills, explore your interests and see how your studies come to life.
Your responsibilities
Support experienced professionals in their daily activities.
Learn and apply new tools or methods relevant to your area of study.
Contribute to small-scale projects under the guidance of your supervisor.
Collaborate with people from diverse backgrounds and share ideas in an international environment.
Your profile
You are currently studying in a physics field.
You are required or encouraged by your university to complete a practical training period.
You are eager to develop your skills through on-the-job learning.
You enjoy teamwork and learning from others in a collaborative setting.
Your skills
Fundamental knowledge in your field of study.
Curiosity, precision and a proactive attitude towards learning.
Good communication skills and ability to work effectively in a multicultural team.

As a motivated young mechanical design engineer, with a specific interest in seeking practical solutions around mechanical systems, CERN's graduate program may very well give you that challenging opportunity.

The mandate of the MME group, within the Engineering Department (EN), is to provide to the CERN community specific engineering solutions combining mechanical design, fabrication and material sciences. Historically the group maintains and develops the know-how on the mechanical construction of beam accelerator components and physics detectors. You will join the Design Office that is in charge of mechanical design of components required for CERN's accelerator and detectors, comprising many high-tech equipment such as superconducting magnets and cavities, vacuum systems and instrumentation. And under the supervision of a senior design engineer, you will design and develop mechanical components and systems from concept to production.
What we offer:
A collaborative and innovative work environment.
Opportunities for professional growth and development.
Access to the latest tools and technologies.
Supportive team culture focused on achieving excellence.
Your responsibilities
Design and develop mechanical components and systems from concept to production.
Create detailed 3D models and 2D drawings using CATIA V5, adhering to ISO GPS norms.
Carry out simple structural analysis and numerical calculations.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams within the group, material science, manufacturing, and quality assurance, to ensure design feasibility and manufacturability.
Continuously improve designs based on feedback and testing results.
Participate in problem-solving and troubleshooting activities related to design and production issues.
Maintain accurate documentation of designs, modifications, and project progress.
Your profile
Initial experience in mechanical design and development of mechanical components or assemblies.
Knowledge of 3D CAD modelling and 2D technical drafting, preferably using CATIA V5
Understanding of mechanical engineering principles, including materials, manufacturing processes and mechanical behaviour of structures.
Skills
Proficiency in CAD software such as CATIA V5 for creating 3D & 2D drawings.
Strong understanding of ISO GPS norms and their application in mechanical design.
Practical knowledge of mechanics and mechanical systems.
Ability to learn new languages (French / English).
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in Mechanical Engineering (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is either a Bachelor's or Master's degree.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.
Applicants without University degree are not eligible.
Applicants with a PhD are not eligible.

Be part of the future of mobility at CERN and lead projects contributing to the delivery and evolution of CERN's mobility strategy. You will coordinate the implementation of the mobility plan, prepare the next mobility plan, and lead cross-functional projects and events that improve mobility across CERN sites.
Your responsibilities:
Coordinate and monitor the actions of CERN's mobility plan through to the 2028 horizon, including milestones, dependencies, risks, decisions and follow-up actions.
Maintain a consolidated project portfolio and ensure regular, reliable reporting on status, priorities, issues and forthcoming decisions.
Work with action owners and stakeholders to translate strategic objectives into practical workplans, deliverables and implementation steps.
Contribute to the preparation of the future CERN mobility plan by gathering needs, analysing lessons learned, structuring consultations and drafting supporting material.
Pilot mobility-related projects and events, from initial scoping and stakeholder alignment through implementation, operational coordination and post-event review.
Participate actively in the CERN mobility working group, prepare inputs and meetings, document conclusions, and coordinate agreed follow-up.
Support communication and stakeholder engagement on mobility initiatives, ensuring that information is clear, timely and adapted to the target audience.
Identify opportunities for service improvement, sustainability and better user experience, and formulate evidence-based recommendations for decision-making.
Ensure that project documentation, decisions, indicators and lessons learned are recorded and accessible for continuity and governance purposes.
Your profile:
Graduated in Project Management, Transport and Mobility, Urban Planning, Sustainability, Engineering, Business Administration, Public Policy or a related field.
Initial experience in project coordination, multi-stakeholder initiatives, mobility, events, sustainability or service development would be an asset.
Experience in an international or multidisciplinary environment would be an advantage.
Skills:
Ability to structure and monitor projects, action plans, milestones, risks and deliverables.
Strong analytical and drafting skills, with the ability to turn varied inputs into concise reports and recommendations.
Good command of common office, collaboration, presentation and project-tracking tools.
Ability to organise meetings, workshops and events and to ensure systematic follow-up.
Interest in sustainable mobility, transport services and user-centred service improvement.
Clear communication and stakeholder management.
Ability to work autonomously while escalating risks and decisions appropriately.
Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the other language.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
You have a professional background in Transportation Management, Civil Engineering (or a related field) and have either:
a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;
or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

En tant que chef ou cheffe de clinique, vous avez obtenu votre titre de spécialiste en infectiologie ou êtes sur le point de finaliser votre formation.
Dans cette fonction, vous assurez l’ensemble des activités cliniques du service et évoluez dans un environnement universitaire stimulant, à l’interface des soins, de l’enseignement et de la recherche. Grâce à votre expertise clinique et à votre capacité d’adaptation, vous intervenez dans les secteurs et unités du service suivant : la consultation d’infectiologie générale, la consultation d’infectiologie ambulatoire, l’orthopédie septique, le HIV, l’infectiologie gériatrique, ainsi que l’infectiologie des patients immunodéprimés.
Sous la supervision d’un médecin adjoint, vous assurez de manière autonome l’évaluation, le diagnostic et le suivi de situations cliniques souvent complexes, tout en apportant un appui spécialisé aux équipes médico-soignantes. Vous mobilisez votre sens clinique, votre esprit d’analyse et votre capacité de décision afin de garantir une prise en charge de qualité, fondée sur les meilleures pratiques médicales.
Grâce à votre sens de l’organisation et à votre aptitude à gérer les priorités, vous conduisez efficacement vos activités cliniques tout en répondant aux nombreuses sollicitations liées à votre fonction (patients et patientes, téléphones, correspondances, réunions). Vous veillez au respect des procédures institutionnelles et contribuez activement à l’amélioration continue de la qualité et de la sécurité des soins.
Face à des situations exigeantes et à la diversité des problématiques rencontrées, vous faites preuve de discernement, de résilience et d’une excellente gestion du stress. Votre curiosité intellectuelle et votre intérêt pour l’évolution des connaissances médicales vous permettent de maintenir un haut niveau d’expertise.
Évoluant au sein d’une équipe pluridisciplinaire, vous collaborez étroitement avec les différents services, ainsi que les professionnels et professionnelles de l’institution dans une approche coordonnée et centrée sur les besoins des patientes et patients. Vous entretenez des relations de travail constructives et favorisez une communication claire, respectueuse et adaptée avec vos collègues, les personnes prises en charge et leurs proches.
En vous appuyant sur votre esprit d’équipe, vous faites preuve de solidarité face aux imprévus. En tant que cheffe ou chef de clinique, vous participez activement à la supervision et à la formation des médecins internes du service, en adoptant une posture de mentorat et en partageant votre expertise.
Par ailleurs, vous avez la possibilité de participer à des projets de recherche en cours au sein du service.

En tant que médecin interne, vous avez débuté votre parcours de formation en médecine interne et souhaitez désormais vous orienter vers l’obtention du titre de spécialiste en infectiologie.
Dans ce contexte, vous rejoignez le Service des maladies infectieuses et participez aux activités des différentes consultations spécialisées, notamment en maladies infectieuses générales, auprès des personnes immunodéprimées, des personnes âgées, dans le domaine de l’orthopédie septique et du VIH/Sida, au travers de rotations.
Sous la supervision des médecins cadres, vous assurez la prise en charge des patientes et patients qui vous sont confiés, tant en ambulatoire qu’en intrahospitalier, au sein de l’ensemble de l’institution. Vous développez progressivement votre expertise clinique en étant confronté et confrontée à des situations variées et parfois complexes, qui renforcent vos capacités d’analyse, votre jugement clinique et votre aptitude à vous adapter rapidement à de nouveaux contextes médicaux.
Grâce à votre sens de l’organisation et à votre rigueur, vous assurez les activités cliniques, diagnostiques et thérapeutiques nécessaires à la prise en charge des patientes et patients. Vous veillez au respect des règles et des procédures internes, dans un souci constant de qualité des prestations médicales apportées.
Face à la diversité des demandes de consultation et à la complexité de certaines situations cliniques, vous faites preuve de sang-froid, de discernement et d’une bonne gestion du stress. Votre curiosité intellectuelle vous incite à approfondir vos connaissances et à comprendre les enjeux des situations auxquelles vous faites face. Vous accueillez également les retours constructifs avec ouverture et les utilisez comme leviers de progression dans l’atteinte de vos objectifs de formation.
Évoluant dans un environnement universitaire stimulant et exigeant, au sein d’une équipe pluridisciplinaire, vous participez également à la formation des médecins stagiaires. Vous collaborez étroitement avec l’ensemble des équipes médico-soignantes de l’institution, dans une approche proactive et centrée sur les besoins des patientes et patients. Vous veillez à maintenir une communication claire, respectueuse et adaptée, tant avec vos collègues qu’avec les personnes prises en charge et leurs proches.
Par ailleurs, vous avez la possibilité de participer à des projets de recherche en cours au sein du service.
Dans le cadre de votre parcours de formation, vous développez vos compétences conformément au plan de formation et aux exigences de la FMH durant trois années au sein du service. Celui-ci offre un environnement reconnu pour la qualité de son enseignement, un large éventail d’activités en infectiologie ainsi que des opportunités de développement favorisant l’obtention du titre FMH. Vous bénéficiez également d’un accompagnement personnalisé grâce à des séances de coaching, des formations ciblées et un encadrement régulier assuré par les médecins cadres ainsi que les chefs et cheffes de clinique.

The BE-EA-DC section is responsible of mechanical beamline equipment such as beam intercepting devices and beam instrumentations. This equipment requires constant maintenance and upgrading to ensure its reliability and accuracy.
Your responsibilities
Conduct the dismantling/assembling activities of the beam line equipment.
Actively participate in all stages of the mechanical equipment readiness, from production to installation.
Collaborate closely with engineers, coordination teams, technicians.
Communicate and report the advancement of the work to the supervisor and project managers.
Participate to various mechanical design studies (new beam line equipment, tooling, upgrade).
Write technical specifications and procedures (maintenance, installation).
Maintain up to date and improve the equipment maintenance database.
More information here.
Your profile
Hands-on experience with mechanical equipment assembly and installation.
Experience reading 2D drawings (ISO-GPS).
Familiarity with 3D modeling software (CATIA) and Microsoft Office pack.
Familiarity with a Computerized Maintenance Management System.
Skills
Understanding of the design of mechanical equipment and structures.
Knowledge of manufacturing methods and work preparation (procedures, orders, BOM, metrology, logistics... ).
Knowledge of design codes and compliance verification of mechanical equipment.
Organisation, planning and control of tasks.
Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the basics of the other language.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in Mechanical Engineering (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is a general secondary education diploma.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.
Applicants with a Bachelor's, Master's or PhD degree are not eligible.

La DAI recherche un ou une auditrice interne pour compléter son équipe composée de 6 auditeurs et auditrices internes.
Dans ce cadre, vous avez comme principales missions de planifier, conduire et documenter les missions d’audit selon la méthodologie définie. Vous identifiez et analysez les risques et vous évaluez le système de contrôle interne mis en place par les HUG pour les limiter.
Vous rédigez des rapports d’audit pertinents, clairs et succincts avec des recommandations apportant une valeur ajoutée puis vous assurez un suivi des recommandations émises.
Vous informez régulièrement le Directeur de la DAI sur le déroulement de vos activités et les faits importants constatés. Vous présentez clairement et succinctement les rapports et constatations au Directeur de la DAI ainsi qu’aux responsables des domaines audités.
Par ailleurs, vous êtes une personne référente à l’interne pour toute question, information, documentation liée aux procédures et directives institutionnelles ainsi qu’au cadre légal cantonal ou fédéral.
Enfin, vous contribuez à la simplification des processus internes en faisant valoir l’intelligence collective.
Vous avez un intérêt marqué par le domaine de la gestion hospitalière au sein d’un hôpital universitaire et souhaitez participer directement à l’amélioration continue de la prise en charge des patients et patientes et de la qualité des soins.

Strong leadership, mentoring, and research team management skills.

Background in molecular engineering, cell-based assays, and translational research.

Preferred

Familiarity with IND-enabling studies and early development.

Experience engaging with senior leadership and external stakeholders.

We are seeking an experienced CAR Engineer/Immunologist to help develop next-generation engineered cell therapies. This role combines molecular immunology, synthetic biology, receptor engineering, and cellular engineering to advance innovative therapeutic programs.

Design and optimize next-generation CARs to enhance specificity, activation, persistence, safety, and therapeutic efficacy.

Engineer and characterize CARs across multiple immune-cell types.

Develop and lead in vitro assays to assess cell phenotype, signaling, cytotoxicity, proliferation, and persistence.

Analyze complex datasets and establish scalable platforms to accelerate CAR discovery.

Mentor and lead a team of scientists while contributing to scientific strategy, patents, publications, and presentations.

PhD, MD/PhD, or equivalent in Immunology, Molecular Biology, Bioengineering, or a related field.

Experience in CAR-T, CAR-NK, CAR-M, or related cell therapy technologies.

Strong expertise in molecular immunology, immune-cell biology, and CAR/receptor engineering.

Experience with immune-cell functional assays and one or more delivery/editing platforms such as lentiviral vectors, LNP/mRNA delivery, or CRISPR-based technologies.

Proven scientific leadership, project ownership, and team management experience.

Preferred

Experience with advanced CAR designs, including multispecific, logic-gated, armored, or inducible CARs.

Knowledge of immune profiling, flow cytometry, and single-cell analysis.

Experience in solid tumor immunology and tumor microenvironment research.

Strong record of innovation through publications, patents, or therapeutic program development.

Experience presenting to and collaborating with senior leadership and external stakeholders.

/job/Basel/Clinical-Pharmacology-Lead---.description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position
In Roche’s Pharmaceutical Research and Early Development organisation (pRED), we make transformative medicines for patients in order to tackle some of the world’s toughest unmet healthcare needs. At pRED, we are united by our mission to transform science into medicines. Together, we create a culture defined by curiosity, responsibility, and humility, where our talented people are empowered and inspired to bring forward extraordinary, life-changing innovation at speed.

At the intersection of science and innovation, pRED’s Pharmaceutical Sciences (PS) organisation enables the discovery and development of safe and effective therapeutics at optimal doses in relevant populations with a vision to power translation, continuously improve the accuracy of our predictions and accelerate the development of tomorrow's medicines. By seamlessly integrating our three core pillars—Translational Safety, Translational Pharmacology, and Biomarkers—we drive end-to-end asset development across the entire value chain, from target assessment to on-market support. Our mission is to continuously improve predictive accuracy, optimise dosing strategies for the right patient populations, and accelerate the development of tomorrow's safe and effective therapeutics. 

Within the Clinical Pharmacology Section in the Quantitative Clinical Pharmacology Department, this position operates globally, is deeply embedded within cross-functional matrix project teams and can support multiple of Roche's focus disease areas (CVRM, Immunology, Neuroscience, Oncology and Ophthalmology).

The Opportunity

In this role, you will lead the scientific advancement of clinical programs by serving as the core quantitative and clinical pharmacology lead within cross-functional project teams. You will drive all aspects of Clinical Pharmacology (CP) across all development phases and strategically apply Model-Informed Drug Development (MIDD) approaches to optimise trial designs, justify dose selections, inform development decisions and mitigate risks across both early and late-stage development. Your scope will be modality-agnostic, giving you oversight that spans small molecules, large molecules, and novel platforms. 

Strategic & Quantitative Plan Execution: Actively contribute to the development of clinical development strategies, including the design of clinical trials and lead the development, implementation, and execution of the Clinical Pharmacology and MIDD strategies for assigned assets across all development phases. Translate Clinical Pharmacology principles into predictive models that guide dose/regimen selection, drug-drug interactions (DDI), special population strategies, pediatric extrapolations and geographic/ethnic bridging.
Modelling & Simulation Mastery: Apply pharmacometric methodologies (such as population PK/PD, PBPK, or QSP) to perform clinical trial simulations, characterise exposure-response relationships, and define quantitative criteria for early, data-driven go/no-go decisions. You bring proficiency in pharmacometric software (e.g., NONMEM, R, SimCyp, MATLAB). 
Regulatory & Asset Maximisation: Lead the CP sections of major regulatory documents (including IB, IND, PIP, PSP, NDA, BLA). Ensure high-quality, fit-for-purpose submission documents using Roche initiatives like lean development authoring and digital submission excellence. Represent the company as a subject matter expert in health authority interactions.
Business Development: Provide clinical and quantitative pharmacology expertise during due diligence for in-licensing and out-licensing activities.
Digital Innovation: Proactively develop and incorporate AI/ML methodologies into Clinical Pharmacology activities and day-to-day quantitative workflows to optimise data interpretation and efficiency.
Matrix Influence & Resilience: Work effectively across a complex, global matrix organisation. Address conflicts with high resilience and foster an environment of challenger safety where diverse scientific views are valued.
Mentorship: Guide and mentor junior scientists within the department to foster strategic and technical growth and professional development.

 
Who You Are

Education: You hold a PhD, Pharm.D., or MD with a specialisation in Pharmacometrics, Clinical Pharmacology, or a related scientific discipline.
Experience: You bring 5+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical or biotech industry in the area of Quantitative Clinical Pharmacology. You have a strong understanding of drug discovery and clinical development, including biology and disease knowledge, and you bring a proven track record of applying Model-Informed Drug Development (MIDD) principles. 
Technical Toolkit: You have a strong foundation in Clinical Pharmacology principles and quantitative drug development, with a solid understanding and experience in applying advanced quantitative modelling (proven proficiency in core pharmacometric software/tool kits such as NONMEM, R or Simcyp), data analytics, and emerging AI-enabled approaches to support evidence-based decision-making. You understand the regulatory landscape and how to integrate diverse data to optimise development.
Communication: You have outstanding communication skills and a clear ability to translate complex quantitative data into actionable strategic messages for cross-functional leadership.
Matrix Influence & Resilience:  You demonstrate strategic thinking,  matrix flexibility and high resilience, working effectively across global organisations to handle conflicts and foster an environment of challenger safety where diverse scientific views are valued.

At Roche, we aim high to deliver life-changing healthcare solutions. If you’re ready to make a meaningful impact on patients and healthcare systems worldwide, this is the place for you.

 
 Where pay transparency applies, details are provided based on the primary posting location. For this role, the primary location is Basel. If you are interested in additional locations where the role may be available, we will provide the relevant compensation details later in the hiring process.

Who we are
A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.

Let’s build a healthier future, together.

Roche is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

/job/Warsaw/Data-Scientist_202609-122958.description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position
Data Scientist

Roche Digital Technology (RDT) is where innovation meets purpose. 

As a global team at the heart of Roche, we are a community of business-minded technologists committed to help shape tomorrow’s digital future of healthcare. Our mission is to power Roche through cutting-edge digital technologies, harnessing the potential of artificial intelligence, data, and scalable tech innovations. Driven by purpose and passion, we’re building a future where digital is a core strength across all of Roche, enabling smarter ways of working, unlocking human potential, and driving breakthroughs that truly matter for millions of patients around the world. 

You'll work alongside curious, ambitious technologists who value ownership, rigour, and fast, visible impact over process for its own sake. Rather than settling into one fixed lane, you'll move with the work as priorities shift, growing your expertise across a genuinely wide range of problems. If you want your day-to-day work to reach millions of patients and to help shape what a still-emerging technology looks like in practice, this is a rare moment to join at the ground floor.

At Roche, we offer a hybrid work model that combines flexibility with in-person collaboration. For now, we require our employees to be in our Warsaw or Poznań office on average two days per week. The specific office days may vary depending on business needs, such as workshops, conferences, town halls, team meetings, and other collaborative events.

The opportunity: 

Roche's AI Function builds the platforms, tools, and data science muscle that let teams across Roche turn AI, GenAI, and agentic ideas into real products, fast. We make it safe, simple, and scalable to build with LLMs, enterprise data, and orchestration, so experimentation stops staying experimental and starts driving real business value. And now we're pushing further into agentic AI: systems that reason, plan, and act on their own, under human oversight. Join us and help define how Roche builds, evaluates, and governs that next generation of AI at enterprise scale.

The kind of work you'll do 
Build and ship
Design and ship AI/ML solutions, from prototype to a monitored capability people actually depend on, including Roche's next generation of agentic AI: systems that plan and execute complex, multi-step work autonomously. Work closely with product owners, engineers, and business stakeholders throughout.
Turn ambiguous problems into clear modelling approaches, and explain the trade-offs in language anyone can follow. Choose the right tool for the problem: a classical model, a fine-tuned model, retrieval over a foundation model or an agentic workflow, rather than reaching for an LLM by default.
Write clean, production-ready, reproducible code, and help shape the reusable patterns the wider team relies on.
Bring rigour
Bring rigour to every experiment. Solid baselines, held-out testing, real error analysis. No shortcuts.
Treat evaluation as core craft, not an afterthought. Build eval sets and harnesses for GenAI systems, use golden datasets and regression checks for prompts, and statistically evaluate outputs for safety, reliability and consistency, offline and in production.
Root solutions in real user feedback, not just lab results.
Measure and inform
Power decisions with analytics. Surface the cost, value, adoption, and usage data that tells AI leadership what's working and where to invest next.
Govern and share
Build within Roche's governance, security, and compliance guardrails, from day one of a project to the last.
Contribute to those guardrails in practice: help design the checks that help embed fairness, explainability and privacy into pipelines so they are enforced rather than aspirational.
Share what you learn through reviews, demos, and onboarding docs. No lesson stays siloed.

Who you are :

Technical depth
Hands-on expertise in data science and software engineering. Python, LLMs, RAG pipelines, agentic workflows. Equally comfortable writing production code, designing system architecture, or setting integration standards.
Evaluate and fine-tune pre-trained models for domain use. Design RAG and search/synthesis architectures. Build evaluation harnesses and statistically evaluate outputs for safety, reliability, and consistency.
Strong NLP foundations: preprocessing, language modelling, sentiment analysis, NER.
A solid core in statistics, model evaluation, feature engineering and standard algorithms
Real depth on vector embeddings, search theory, and vector database selection and architecture, along with prompt and context engineering.

Strategic and operational range
Comfortable moving from strategic roadmap planning to solving ad-hoc technical problems on the ground. Skilled at bridging non-technical stakeholders and technical implementation.
Comfortable building MLOps/LLMOps pipelines for continuous deployment and monitoring, including observability for LLM systems (tracing, tokens, latency, cost telemetry and drift and hallucination monitoring). 
Comfortable forecasting and optimising infrastructure and API costs, and managing platform vendor relationships to keep tools interoperable, secure, and future-proof.
Communication
Strong written and verbal English, with the ability to explain technical trade-offs to technical and non-technical audiences alike.
A learning posture that keeps pace with a fast-changing field, with enthusiasm for knowledge-sharing.  
Preferred/nice to have:
Hands-on experience deploying enterprise AI solutions on AWS or Azure (GCP exposure a plus).
Model risk management, fairness and bias mitigation, transparency, explainability, and data privacy.
Pharma, healthcare, or financial services, including GxP compliance and handling sensitive information, plus awareness of emerging compliance standards for GenAI and foundation models.

What You Get
Salary Range: 170’100.00 - 243’000.00 - 315’900.00 PLN Annual based on an employment contract (Umowa o Pracę).
Annual Performance Bonus: Target bonus of 15% based on performance.
Dedicated Training Budget: Funding for certifications, AI/tech courses, global conferences, and diversified career paths.
Recharge Fridays: 2 additional paid Fridays off per quarter available to completely disconnect.
Take Time Program: Up to 3 months of sabbatical leave to use for any personal purpose.
Flex Location: Freedom to work remotely from different global locations for specified periods throughout the year.
Take Time for Charity: Up to 2 weeks of additional paid leave to engage in volunteering initiatives.
Comprehensive Benefits: Private healthcare (LuxMed packages), group life insurance (UNUM), MultiSport card, and vacation subsidy.
Stock & Tech Perks: Roche stock share purchase program, yearly sales of company laptops and cars, and much more!

Apply directly and join us in shaping the future of healthcare.
If you feel this offer suits a friend of yours, feel free to share it.
Want to know what it’s like to be a part of Roche IT first-hand? Check out our blog!
