Beyond driving core execution, our team architects pioneering, multi-molecule platform frameworks, enables best-in-class technical practices, and upskills the broader CMC organization—transforming how device technology reaches patients worldwide.

The Opportunity
Are you passionate about not only driving high-impact portfolio strategies, but also fostering a collaborative organizational culture that empowers connected teams to deliver their best work? Do you want to directly shape global regulatory policy while upskilling an entire CMC regulatory organization?
Architect and drive global regulatory strategy for complex technologies, including drug-device combination products, novel gene/cell therapy delivery systems, and standalone physical devices. Integrate multi-disciplinary regulatory domains across technical device lifecycle management, pharma CMC drug frameworks, and clinical device domains to ensure seamless execution of the regulatory strategy. 
Champion scalable, portfolio-enabling device platform strategies that accelerate development timelines and drive efficiency across multiple pipeline molecules.
Partner closely with key internal stakeholders across Pharma Technical, Pharma Development, Global Pharma Procurement/Supply, Research & Early Development, and Roche Diagnostics.
Provide strategic risk management, regulatory guidance, and high-level decision-making to solve high-impact challenges in alignment with business objectives. Deliver senior-level device regulatory consultation to ensure alignment with global health authority expectations.
Represent Roche Pharma in key external policy venues, engaging directly with global Health Authorities to shape regulatory policy and industry standards.
Author and disseminate strategic external positions through trade groups, international working groups, industry presentations, and publications.
Build internal device regulatory capabilities and evolve operating models, processes, and systems to support rapid device innovation.

Who You Are
You are a visionary and agile regulatory strategist who thrives in dynamic matrix environments. You excel at applying holistic systems thinking to navigate complex, ambiguous regulatory landscapes and possess executive-level communication skills to align senior leaders and cross-functional partners. As a collaborative leader and mentor, you are dedicated to building organizational capabilities, fostering trust, and driving a high-performance team culture.

Bachelor's degree in engineering, or a related scientific discipline (advanced degree is preferred).
Minimum 15 years of experience in regulatory affairs, drug development, or technical development within the biopharmaceutical/medical device industry.
Primary focus and extensive global regulatory strategy expertise in drug-device combination products and pharmaceutical/biologic CMC frameworks across the full product lifecycle.
Proven track record of successful health authority interactions, negotiations, and major global drug approvals.
Demonstrated experience building trusted relationships with global regulators, health authorities, and trade associations to shape external regulatory policies.
Willingness and ability to travel up to 10%.

The ideal location for this role is East Hanover, NJ but remote work may be possible (there may be some restrictions based on legal entity). Please note that this role would not provide relocation as a result. If associate is remote, all home office expenses and any travel/lodging to specific East Hanover, NJ site for periodic live meetings will be at the employee’s expense. The expectation of working hours and travel (domestic and/or international) will be defined by the hiring manager. This position will require 15% travel.

The Insights and Analytics team is dedicated to enabling improved decision making at Novartis by leveraging superior data and advanced analytics capabilities to generate actionable insights that drive business growth and enhanced performance. We collaborate closely with the US business, bringing insights and challenging ideas to empower smarter, data-driven decision-making.

Reporting into the Executive Director, Targeting and Field Intelligence, the Director, Targeting & Field Intelligence – Pipeline & Portfolio serves as the Horizontal Integration Leader across TNBA, responsible for advancing Novartis' enterprise field intelligence strategy and enabling a unified approach to field direction, customer engagement, and decision support.

While Therapeutic Area Targeting Directors serve as Vertical Business Leaders accountable for stakeholder management and TA-specific outcomes, this role is accountable for enterprise prioritization, cross-portfolio capability development, operational consistency, and the evolution of a unified field intelligence ecosystem across brands, field functions, and channels.

The role is accountable for advancing the Integrated Intelligence Layer that powers portfolio capabilities like Dynamic Targeting, Next Best Actions, Unified Field Direction, and Field Orchestration across Novartis. This leader ensures field teams receive consistent, actionable, and personalized guidance that improves customer engagement, field effectiveness, and business outcomes.

 
Job Description
 
Key Responsibilities:
1. Enterprise Field Intelligence & Orchestration
Lead the evolution of enterprise field intelligence capabilities including Dynamic Targeting, NBA, field direction, and orchestration.
Establish a unified approach for connecting targeting, recommendations, account insights, planning, and execution across field teams.
Drive consistent field experiences across Therapeutic Areas while enabling business-specific needs. 
2. Portfolio Strategy & Prioritization
Own portfolio intake, prioritization, capacity planning, and roadmap governance across TNBA.
Consolidate and align requirements across Therapeutic Areas and field functions.
Drive enterprise prioritization decisions based on business value, scalability, impact, and delivery capacity. 
3. Cross-Portfolio Capability Leadership
Lead enterprise initiatives that span multiple Therapeutic Areas, including Dynamic Targeting, Field Orchestration, MSL targeting, and future field intelligence capabilities.
Develop reusable frameworks, common requirements, and scalable deployment approaches.
Partner with cross-functional teams to accelerate adoption and maximize reuse. 
4. Governance, Standards & Operational Excellence
Establish common governance, standards, and processes for targeting, NBA, prioritization, and capability deployment.
Simplify ways of working through standardized frameworks, improved transparency, and reduced operational complexity.
Strengthen coordination and execution across US and HYD teams. 
5. AI & Operating Model Transformation
Identify and implement opportunities to improve productivity, speed, and quality through AI, automation, and process redesign.
Drive continuous improvement of TNBA's operating model and enterprise capabilities.
Enable scalable, data-driven execution across the portfolio.

Novartis seeks an individual with extensive experience in strategic leadership and customer engagement within the pharmaceutical or healthcare industry. This role requires a deep understanding of customer targeting strategies and the ability to align these with broader organizational goals. The candidate should have a proven track record of guiding teams in identifying and prioritizing customers and assessing patient growth opportunities. Experience in reviewing, enhancing targeting methods, and implementing Next Best Action models is crucial for driving engagement and achieving business objectives.

Essential Requirements:
Advanced degree in Business Administration, Data Science, Analytics, or a related field
Minimum 8+ years of experience in customer prioritization, analytics, or strategic planning within the pharmaceutical or healthcare industry
Proven track record of developing and implementing strategic goals and targets for large field teams
Ability to inspire and guide cross-functional teams towards achieving strategic objectives
Excellent analytical skills, with the ability to interpret complex data and translate insights into actionable strategies
Experience in collaborating with senior leadership to align field goals with broader business objectives
Strong understanding of market dynamics, competitive landscape, and industry trends in pharmaceuticals
Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively liaise between field teams and senior management
Demonstrated ability to foster a culture of continuous improvement and data-driven decision-making
Proficiency in using advanced analytics tools and technologies to support goal setting and performance evaluation

Novartis Compensation Summary:
The salary for this position is expected to range between $185,500.00 and $ 344,500.00.

The final salary offered is determined based on factors like, but not limited to, relevant skills and experience, and upon joining Novartis will be reviewed periodically. Novartis may change the published salary range based on company and market factors.

Your compensation will include a performance-based cash incentive and, depending on the level of the role, eligibility to be considered for annual equity awards.
US-based eligible employees will receive a comprehensive benefits package that includes health, life and disability benefits, a 401(k) with company contribution and match, and a variety of other benefits. In addition, employees are eligible for a generous time off package including vacation, personal days, holidays and other leaves.

Job Description SummaryThe Patent Attorney II will lead and manage designated patent and related intellectual property (IP) activities within the Novartis research and development (R&D) organization.

This role is based out of our San Diego or Cambridge office 3x/week.

 
Job Description
Job responsibilities:
Provide clear, strategic, and business-focused counsel to Novartis R&D clients on invention protection, portfolio development, publication strategy, and third-party risks. 
Build and manage patent portfolios for Novartis R&D projects by identifying inventions and preparing, prosecuting, maintaining, and defending patent filings across areas such as new molecular entities, processes, manufacturing, platforms, technologies, and clinical developments. 
Render legal opinions on patentability, validity, and freedom to operate, and develop patent strategies that strengthen IP positions, support freedom to operate, and enable effective IP defense. 
Apply deep knowledge of national patent law and practice, including relevant legal developments and patent trends, to shape strategy and advice. 
Understand and apply other forms of exclusivity protection, as appropriate. 
Communicate effectively with colleagues and leaders across the legal, IP, and R&D organizations. 
Build and manage relationships with outside counsel and collaborators, including extensive interaction within a multicultural global patent function. 
Conduct due diligence and provide counsel based on those assessments, including freedom-to-operate, infringement, validity, risk evaluation, and risk mitigation strategies. 
Provide IP support for transactional matters, including M&A, research collaborations, and in-licensing opportunities, with advice on contract drafting and negotiation.

Essential requirements:
J.D. degree, admission to at least one state bar, and registration to practice before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office. AND
Advanced degree (Ph.D. strongly preferred) in chemistry or a closely related field (e.g., organic chemistry, medicinal chemistry, chemical engineering) and preferably with 1–2 years of exposure to drug discovery and development processes used in pharmaceutical and/or biotechnology companies. 
7+ years of experience as a qualified patent attorney in a law firm or within the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.
Strong technical expertise in chemistry, preferably including experience with small molecules, synthesis, or pharmaceutical development.
Expertise in U.S. and PCT patent law, filing processes, and prosecution practice, with a detailed understanding of European patent law and other major global patent systems.
Strong client-service orientation, with the ability to build and sustain effective partnerships with key stakeholders and project teams.

Desirable requirements:
Strong analytical, presentation, and communication skills.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively both independently and collaboratively.
Strong research, critical thinking, and decision-making skills, with close attention to detail and a commitment to consistently accurate work.
Excellent organizational and time-management skills, with the flexibility, creativity, and resourcefulness to manage multiple competing priorities successfully.
Strong interpersonal skills, including partnership building, influence, persuasion, and teamwork.

Benefits & Rewards
The salary for this position is expected to range between $185,500 and $344,500 per year. The final salary offered is determined based on factors like, but not limited to, relevant skills and experience, and upon joining Novartis will be reviewed periodically. Novartis may change the published salary range based on company and market factors. Your compensation will include a performance-based cash incentive and, depending on the level of the role, eligibility to be considered for annual equity awards. US-based eligible employees will receive a comprehensive benefits package that includes health, life and disability benefits, a 401(k) with company contribution and match, and a variety of other benefits. In addition, employees are eligible for a generous time off package including vacation, personal days, holidays and other leaves.

/job/DE---Cologne---REMOTE/R77028-Senior.description:
Senior Manager, Account Management (Licensing)

Location: Cologne - Remote

As the Senior Manager, Account Management (Licensing), you will fulfill a critical and exciting role to ensure that all collaborations established under the technology out-licensing business model of Lonza Oss are nurtured well to deliver their full potential. Together with the rest of the Alliance Management Team, this role is expected to maintain and grow existing relationships, negotiate and coordinate contracts, facilitate (new) research, conduct progress monitoring and status reporting.

What you will get:  
An agile career and dynamic working culture. 
An inclusive and ethical workplace. 
Compensation programs that recognize high performance. 
A variety of benefits dependent on role and location. 
The full list of our global benefits can be found here:  https://www.lonza.com/careers/benefits. 

The full-time annual base pay for this position in Germany is expected to range between 77.250,- EUR and 108.150,- EUR. Initial salary placement within this range will be determined based on role‑related factors such as experience, qualifications, and expected contribution. 

What you will do: 
Overseeing the governance of the partnership/license agreements and managing contractual obligations (including implementing and supporting committees; setting meeting agenda's and ensure preparedness for meetings; support formulation of and agree on clear objectives; facilitate decision making and subsequent implementation of agreed actions).
Tracking and ensuring efficient progress towards agreed goals.
Strong focus on increasing alignment, mutual understanding, and trust between collaboration participants (including how the company is perceived by the partner, and how the partnership is perceived by people within Synaffix). Cultivate relationships that support cementing the performance of collaborations and managing of associated internal and external communications.
Identifying the important value drivers and key risks, ensuring those involved do not lose focus on strategic aspects, leading efforts to mitigate risks and accelerate value creation.
Anticipating upcoming changes in project stages or collaboration participants, managing transitions smoothly, and serving as the partnership’s memory, as well as facilitating complex discussions with the partner to map a way forward when unanticipated situations or corporate decisions within either party trigger the need for change.

What we are looking for:
Master’s degree in the field of Life Sciences or equivalent
5-10 years relevant work experience (Life Science, CDMO, Biotech, Pharma)
2 years experience with licensing agreements
Ability to navigate complex licensing contracts and technical information
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work autonomously
English Business Fluent
Ability to travel to visit clients (globally) and Lonza facilities (mainly within Europe)
Strong relationship management and commercial acumen
Skilled in structured problem-solving and escalation management
Excellent communication skills (written and verbal)
Comfort working cross-functionally and internationally
Ability to represent Lonza credibly with senior external stakeholders

About Lonza 

Lonza Oss is a biotech company with a clinical-stage platform technology that enables best-in-class antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), bispecific antibodies and other targeted therapeutics under a technology out-licensing business model. 

At Lonza, our people are our greatest strength. With 30+ sites across five continents, our globally connected teams work together every day to manufacture the medicines of tomorrow. Our core values of Collaboration, Accountability, Excellence, Passion and Integrity reflect who we are and how we work together. Everyone’s ideas, big or small, have the potential to improve millions of lives, and that’s the kind of work we want you to be part of. 
Innovation thrives when people from all backgrounds bring their unique perspectives to the table. At Lonza, we value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. If you’re ready to help turn our customers’ breakthrough ideas into viable therapies, we look forward to welcoming you on board. 

Ready to shape the future of life sciences? Apply now.

Der Arbeitsort dieser Stelle befindet sich in Visp, Schweiz. Anspruchsberechtigten Bewerbern und ihren Familien steht bei Bedarf Unterstützung beim Umzug zur Verfügung.

Zur Verstärkung unserer QC Nasschemie suchen wir eine engagierte und fachlich versierte Persönlichkeit als Senior QC Scientist. In dieser Rolle übernehmen Sie neben anspruchsvollen analytischen Tätigkeiten im Labor auch technische Verantwortung für definierte Methoden und Fachgebiete. Sie unterstützen den Laborleiter bei der Sicherstellung eines effizienten, GMP-konformen Laborbetriebs und fungieren als dessen Vertretung bei Abwesenheit

Was auf Sie wartet:

Eine agile Karriere und eine dynamische Arbeitskultur.

Ein integratives und ethisches Arbeitsumfeld.

Vergütungsprogramme, die hohe Leistung anerkennen.

Eine Vielzahl von Vorteilen, abhängig von Funktion und Standort.
Die vollständige Liste unserer globalen Vorteile finden Sie hier: https://www.lonza.com/careers/benefits.

Ihre Aufgaben:

Selbstständige Durchführung komplexer analytischer Prüfungen und methodenbezogener Tätigkeiten im QC-Labor.

Übernahme der fachlichen Verantwortung für definierte Analysenmethoden, Geräte oder Fachgebiete.

Unterstützung des Laborleiters bei der Organisation und Koordination der täglichen Laboraktivitäten.

Wahrnehmung der Stellvertreterfunktion des Laborleiters und Unterstützung bei operativen sowie technischen Fragestellungen.

Sicherstellung einer termingerechten, qualitativ hochwertigen und GMP-konformen Bereitstellung von Analysenergebnissen.

Unterstützung bei der Bearbeitung von Abweichungen, OOS-/OOT-Ergebnissen, CAPAs und Change Controls.

Fachliche Begleitung von Methodenvalidierungen, Methodenverifizierungen und Methodentransfers.

Durchführung von Fehleranalysen und Troubleshooting bei analytischen oder methodischen Herausforderungen.

Identifikation und Umsetzung von Verbesserungen im Bereich analytischer Methoden, Prozesse und Arbeitsabläufe.

Unterstützung von Audits, Inspektionen sowie behördlichen Anfragen im Verantwortungsbereich.

Förderung einer hohen Datenintegrität sowie der Einhaltung von GMP- und Qualitätsanforderungen.

Fachliche Unterstützung und Coaching von Mitarbeitenden bei methodenbezogenen Fragestellungen.

Was wir suchen:

Abgeschlossenes Studium der Chemie, Biochemie, Pharmazie, Life Sciences oder einer vergleichbaren naturwissenschaftlichen Fachrichtung.

Mehrjährige Berufserfahrung in einem GMP-regulierten QC-Labor.

Fundierte Kenntnisse analytischer Methoden und Laborprozesse.

Erfahrung in Methodenvalidierung, Methodentransfer und analytischem Troubleshooting.

Gute Kenntnisse von GMP-Anforderungen, Datenintegrität und Qualitätssystemen.

Erfahrung im Umgang mit Abweichungen, CAPAs und Change-Control-Prozessen.

Ausgeprägte analytische und konzeptionelle Fähigkeiten sowie eine strukturierte Arbeitsweise.

Hohe Eigenverantwortung, Teamfähigkeit und Kommunikationsstärke.

Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift.

Über Lonza:

Bei Lonza sind unsere Mitarbeiter unsere größte Stärke. An über 30 Standorten auf fünf Kontinenten arbeiten unsere global vernetzten Teams täglich zusammen, um die Medikamente von morgen herzustellen. Unsere Grundwerte: Zusammenarbeit, Verantwortlichkeit, Exzellenz, Leidenschaft und Integrität spiegeln wider, wer wir sind und wie wir zusammenarbeiten. Die Ideen jedes Einzelnen, ob groß oder klein, haben das Potenzial, Millionen von Leben zu verbessern, und genau daran möchten wir Sie teilhaben lassen.

Innovation gedeiht, wenn Menschen unterschiedlichster Herkunft ihre einzigartigen Perspektiven einbringen. Bei Lonza schätzen wir Vielfalt und setzen uns für ein integratives Umfeld für alle Mitarbeiter ein. Wenn Sie bereit sind, die bahnbrechenden Ideen unserer Kunden in praktikable Therapien umzusetzen, freuen wir uns, Sie an Bord begrüßen zu dürfen.

Principal Medical Writer

ICON is a global healthcare intelligence and clinical research organisation united by a mission to bring new medicines and treatments to patients faster.

As a values-driven organisation, integrity, collaboration, agility, and inclusion are at the heart of how we work and interact with each other, customers, patients and suppliers.

We are currently seeking a Principal Medical Writer to join our diverse and dynamic team. As a Principal Medical Writer at ICON, you will be responsible for leading the development of high-quality regulatory and clinical documents that effectively communicate scientific and medical information. Your expertise in medical writing will be crucial in supporting our clients’ submissions to regulatory authorities and ensuring compliance with industry standards.

This role is permanent and is single-client dedicated to a global biotech company

What You Will Be Doing:

Develop regulatory documents for submission to regulatory agencies globally, including Clinical Study Reports, Clinical Summaries of Efficacy and Safety, and Clinical Overviews, in accordance with ICH and other global guidelines, standards and processes, and Incyte authoring standards, as applicable, in adherence with study/project timelines and corporate objectives. 

Manage medical writing projects, including developing timelines (working with the study/project teams, as necessary) and communication with cross-functional team members to maintain awareness of review cycles and expectations. 

Participate in cross-functional meetings to provide input regarding medical writing deliverables, timelines, and any process(es) needed for the completion of regulatory documents. 

Review other documents associated with the assigned project(s) (eg, Protocols and Statistical Analysis Plans), as appropriate. 

#LI-NR1
#LI-Remote

Your Profile:
- A Bachelor's degree in a life science discipline, with Master's degree in life science discipline preferred.
• At least 6 years of medical writing experience in the biopharmaceutical/CRO industry required.
- Regulatory writing experience - Clinical Study Reports, IBs, Protocols 
- Experienced writer who has ideally led submissions in addition to other document experience
- Oncology experience would be a plus
• Proficient understanding and knowledge of domestic and international regulatory requirements required and knowledge of therapeutic areas in all phases of clinical development desired.
• Proficiency in organizing and communicating clinical information necessary.
• Strong communications, organizational, time management, and project management skills are required.

Employment with ICON is contingent upon having the legal right to work in the country where the role is based.

Rewards & Benefits
ICON offers a competitive and comprehensive total rewards package designed to support your health, wellbeing, and career development.

Benefits may include:
Competitive base salary and performance related incentives
Health and wellbeing programmes including medical, dental, and vision coverage where applicable
Retirement and pension plans
Life assurance and disability coverage
Employee assistance programmes and wellbeing resources
Learning and development opportunities through structured training and career pathways

Benefits may vary depending on role and location.

Visit our careers site to read more about the benefits ICON offers.

Inclusion and Accessibility
ICON is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building an inclusive and accessible workplace where everyone feels valued and supported.

If you require reasonable accommodations during the recruitment process, please let us know or submit a request here.

Associate Principal Scientist – Analytical Development (Microbial)

Visp, Schweiz

Der tatsächliche Arbeitsort für diese Position ist Visp, Schweiz. Unterstützung bei der Relocation steht berechtigten Kandidaten und ihren Familien bei Bedarf zur Verfügung.

Möchten Sie die Zukunft innovativer Biopharmazeutika mitgestalten? In dieser Schlüsselrolle übernehmen Sie die wissenschaftliche und technische Verantwortung für die Entwicklung, Implementierung und Validierung moderner bioanalytischer Methoden und treiben gleichzeitig die Digitalisierung und Automatisierung analytischer Labore voran. Ihre Arbeit unterstützt direkt die Entwicklung und Herstellung innovativer biologischer Arzneimittel und ermöglicht die Bereitstellung lebensverändernder Therapien für Patienten weltweit.

Dies ist eine vollständig standortgebundene Position. Die enge Zusammenarbeit vor Ort unterstützt die direkte Abstimmung innerhalb der Teams sowie die wissenschaftliche Präzision, die erforderlich ist, um innovative Therapien nach höchsten Qualitäts- und Sicherheitsstandards zu entwickeln.

Was wir bieten

Eine agile Karriere mit vielfältigen Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten in einem internationalen Umfeld.
Eine inklusive und werteorientierte Unternehmenskultur.
Leistungsorientierte Vergütungsprogramme.
Ein attraktives Leistungs- und Benefitspaket abhängig von Rolle und Standort.
Die vollständige Übersicht unserer globalen Benefits finden Sie hier: https://www.lonza.com/careers/benefits

Ihre Aufgaben

Wissenschaftliche und technische Hauptansprechperson für die Entwicklung, Implementierung und Validierung biochemischer und chromatographischer Assays wie ELISA, Enzym-Assays, RT-qPCR, Protein-PCR, UV/Vis, icIEF sowie RP-, SE- und IEX-HPLC.
Leitung analytischer Entwicklungs-, Transfer- und Validierungsaktivitäten innerhalb mehrerer Studien- und Kundenprogramme.
Erstellung, Überprüfung und finale Freigabe komplexer Studienprotokolle, Arbeitsanweisungen und Berichte gemäß GLP-Anforderungen.
Zusammenarbeit mit funktionsübergreifenden Teams aus Analytical Development, Process Development, Manufacturing und Quality zur Sicherstellung wissenschaftlicher Exzellenz.
Training, Coaching und fachliche Weiterentwicklung von Laborfachkräften und wissenschaftlichen Mitarbeitenden.
Identifikation, Bewertung und Implementierung neuer analytischer Technologien sowie Förderung von Digitalisierungs- und Automatisierungsinitiativen.
Unterstützung kontinuierlicher Verbesserungsprozesse zur Steigerung von Effizienz, Datenqualität und regulatorischer Compliance.

Was wir suchen:

Promotion (PhD) in Biochemie, Biologie, Chemie oder einer vergleichbaren naturwissenschaftlichen Fachrichtung.
Erfahrung in der Entwicklung, Implementierung und Validierung analytischer Methoden im biopharmazeutischen oder pharmazeutischen Umfeld.
Fundierte Kenntnisse moderner bioanalytischer und chromatographischer Technologien wie ELISA, qPCR, icIEF und HPLC.
Fähigkeit, komplexe wissenschaftliche Projekte selbstständig zu leiten und technische Herausforderungen lösungsorientiert zu adressieren.
Ausgeprägte Kommunikations- und Teamfähigkeiten sowie Freude an der Zusammenarbeit in einem dynamischen Umfeld.
Hohe Eigeninitiative, Verantwortungsbewusstsein und strukturierte Arbeitsweise.
Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift.

Über Lonza

Bei Lonza sind unsere Mitarbeitenden unsere größte Stärke. This is a graduate position within the QUEST programme, funded by the EOSC4ALL project of the European Commission. It is open to recent graduates in computer science, engineering or a related field. You do not need to tick every box or have every skill listed below, if you are motivated to learn, we encourage you to apply.
Join CERN's Storage and Data Management Group and help evolve the storage systems behind the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), while learning large-scale storage, cloud-native technologies and open-source software with the support of an experienced team.
You will work on CERNBox, the cloud storage used by the whole CERN community, from scientists to administrative staff. Your main task is to help make it interoperable with research infrastructures across Europe, through the Open Cloud Mesh (OCM) standard, and easy to deploy anywhere using Kubernetes. You will also explore how AI can help users find and use their data.
If you enjoy open standards, open source and building tools that many institutions can adopt, this is the place for you! You will be supported by experienced colleagues and learn from the whole team.
Your responsibilities
Develop and integrate backend and frontend software components.
Package and deploy interoperable services in distributed environments.
Support CERN community: you will join our operations team, troubleshooting incidents and supporting users.
Contribute your code, features and fixes back to the CERNBox open-source projects, working alongside a broader open-source community.
Work with partner institutions and research infrastructures across Europe to test, validate and refine these tools together.
Support users and partner teams as they adopt these tools, helping with troubleshooting and guidance.
Explore and prototype AI/ML capabilities for CERNBox, working with users to identify practical use cases. Prior AI/ML experience is welcome but not required.
Your profile
Experience with backend development in Go, and an interest in full-stack development.
Comfortable working in Linux environments and troubleshooting software and systems.
Familiarity with frontend development, ideally using JavaScript/TypeScript and Vue.js.
Software development experience from studies, projects, internships or open-source contributions, with a willingness to take ownership of features and to collaborate with others.
Ability to collaborate with users, technical teams and external partners.
Interest in open-source software, distributed systems and interoperability.
Skills
Backend: Go and API development.
Frontend: Modern frameworks such as Vue.js or similar technologies.
Systems: Linux, troubleshooting and software integration.
Cloud-native technologies: Containers, Docker, Kubernetes, Helm and CI/CD pipelines are an advantage.
Collaboration: Good communication skills and the ability to work effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
You have a professional background in Computing Engineer (or a related field) and have either:
a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;
or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.

Introduction
The CERN ATLAS Team plays a major role in the construction of the future silicon ATLAS Inner Tracker (ITk). In particular, the CERN Detector Technologies (DT) team focuses on the realisation of the Pixel Outer Barrel for the ITk. Our activities include the design, prototyping and assembly of the support structures and tooling as well as the final detector integration, installation and testing.

As a mechanical engineer in the CERN-DT Team, you will join the Engineering Office Section (EP-DT-EO) and work closely with personnel from the ATLAS Group (EP-ATL) and the Technical Coordination Team of the ATLAS Experiment on the design, construction and installation of the ATLAS ITk Pixel Outer System.
Functions
Design of precision tooling for the integration, testing and installation of the ITk Pixel Outer System Detector, comprising the Outer Barrel, Endcaps and Inner System Support Tube.
Design and develop service installation procedures and tooling, including temporary service management solutions for testing of the ITk Pixel Detector.
Verify the design of components and tooling according to the relevant standards and best engineering practices, performing both, analytical and numerical calculations.
Develop, document and implement tools and procedures for integration and installation of detector components and services.
Participate hands-on in the detector integration work in the ATLAS SR1 cleanroom as well as the preparation on surface and in the cavern for the installation.
Prepare technical specifications for components and tools, following up their production, acceptance and installation.
Support preparation of and participate in the ATLAS ID detector extraction.

You will join the Accelerator and Technology Sector (ATS) which comprises four departments -Beams, Engineering, Accelerator Systems, and Technology - responsible for the Sector's main technical activities.
Within the ATS Directorate Office (ATS-DO), you will join the ATS Project Office, contributing to the communication, dissemination, and outreach activities of the European project EPITA as well as other strategic projects and studies coordinated by ATS.
In this role, you will help promote project achievements to a broad range of stakeholders, including project partners, funding bodies, the scientific community, and the public.
Your responsibilities:

Manage and regularly update the project website (WordPress), including the homepage and the "Latest News" section.

Create engaging communication content, including newsletters, feature articles, social media posts, and audiovisual material.
Support and maintain the project's presence across digital communication channels, including LinkedIn, YouTube, and other relevant platforms.
Produce, collect, and edit photographs and video content showcasing project activities and results.
Design infographics and visual communication materials or coordinate their development with CERN's graphic design service and external providers.
Participate in annual project meetings, work package meetings, and other key events, presenting communication-related activities and results when required.
Contribute to outreach initiatives aimed at increasing awareness and visibility of the project's objectives and achievements.
Attend regular communication coordination meetings within ATS-DO.
In close collaboration with another Graduate in the team, contribute to communication, dissemination, and outreach activities for other major CERN projects and studies managed by the ATS Project Office, according to priorities and operational needs.
Your profile:
Experience in communication related to science, technology and innovation.
Experience with WordPress would be an advantage.
Skills:
Experience of audiovisual software/tools, e.g. CapCut would be an advantage.
Knowledge of Canva would be an advantage.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.
Eligibility criteria:
You are a national of a CERN Member or Associate Member State.
By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in Science Journalism, Communication/Media Production (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is either a Bachelor's or Master's degree.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.
Applicants without University degree are not eligible.
Applicants with a PhD are not eligible.

You will join a small team of experts managing the PostgreSQL and MySQL databases supporting the LHC experiments, accelerator operations and organisation-wide services. You will help build and automate a modern, highly available database platform, with training and mentoring to grow your skills.

Operate and improve production PostgreSQL (and MySQL) databases: troubleshooting, upgrades, migrations, patching and scaling.
Help design, deploy and run highly available database setups with automated failover.
Automate provisioning, configuration and routine operations using scripting and infrastructure tools.

Job Description Summary#LI-Hybrid
Location: Basel, Switzerland or Cambridge, United States (see separate posting)

Ready to shape the future of innovation at Novartis? As a Patent Attorney, you will play a pivotal role in protecting groundbreaking scientific discoveries and enabling life-changing medicines to reach patients worldwide. Partnering closely with R&D teams, you will drive strategic intellectual property decisions, build robust patent portfolios, and navigate complex legal landscapes to safeguard innovation across the product lifecycle.

 
Job Description
Key Responsibilities
Provide clear, strategic, and business-focused counsel to Novartis R&D clients on invention protection, portfolio development, publication strategy, and third-party risks.
Build and manage patent portfolios for Novartis R&D projects by identifying inventions and preparing, prosecuting, maintaining, and defending patent filings across areas such as new molecular entities, processes, manufacturing, platforms, technologies, and clinical developments.
Render legal opinions on patentability, validity, and freedom to operate, and develop patent strategies that strengthen IP positions, support freedom to operate, and enable effective IP defense.
Apply deep knowledge of national patent law and practice, including relevant legal developments and patent trends, to shape strategy and advice.
Understand and apply other forms of exclusivity protection, as appropriate.
Communicate effectively with colleagues and leaders across the legal, IP, and R&D organizations.
Build and manage relationships with outside counsel and collaborators, including extensive interaction within a multicultural global patent function.
Conduct due diligence and provide counsel based on those assessments, including freedom-to-operate, infringement, validity, risk evaluation, and risk mitigation strategies.
Provide IP support for transactional matters, including M&A, research collaborations, and in-licensing opportunities, with advice on contract drafting and negotiation
Ensure high-quality, timely delivery of work aligned with business goals and budgets
 
Essential Requirements
University degree in law, admission to the bar and qualification as a European Patent Attorney / Lawyer
Advanced degree in chemistry or related field, with strong preference for a doctoral degree
Significant experience as a patent attorney within a law firm or pharmaceutical or biotechnology environment
Strong technical expertise in chemistry, preferably including experience with small molecules, synthesis, or pharmaceutical development.
Expertise in U.S. and PCT patent law, filing processes, and prosecution practice, with a detailed understanding of European patent law and other major global patent systems
Proven ability to partner with scientific and business stakeholders to deliver strategic intellectual property advice
Strong analytical, communication, and decision-making skills with high attention to detail
Ability to manage multiple priorities effectively within a fast-paced, global environment
 
Benefits & Rewards 
At Novartis, we’re committed to reimagining medicine together - and rewarding the people who make it happen. 
  
Expected Annual Base Salary Range for role: CHF 126.000 - CHF 234.000
  
The base salary offered is determined based on gender-neutral objectives, such as relevant skills, competencies and experience in accordance with the Novartis pay setting policy and upon joining Novartis will be reviewed periodically. 
  
The rewards of being part of our team go far beyond base pay and incentives. We also offer a variety of competitive benefits in kind to help you thrive personally and professionally, such as insurance plans, retirement plans, wellbeing resources and global recognition programs. In addition, we provide flexible and hybrid working options, where possible, and minimum 14 weeks paid parental leave. 
 
In addition to your base salary, you may be eligible for a performance-based bonus depending on certain performance parameters. Further details will be provided during the application process.  
  
Read our brochure to learn more about our global total rewards offering: 
https://www.novartis.com/sites/novartis_com/files/novartis-life-handbook.pdf 
  
Note: Benefits and compensation may vary by country and are subject to local legal requirements, including provisions of collective bargaining agreements where applicable. A full overview of your compensation package, including any relevant collective bargaining agreement details applicable to your role based on your employment location and Novartis employer entity, will be communicated separately to you during the application process. 
 
Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion:
Novartis is committed to building an outstanding, inclusive work environment and diverse teams representative of the patients and communities we serve.
 
Accessibility and Accommodation:
Novartis is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodation to all individuals. If, because of a medical condition or disability, you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the recruitment process, or in order to receive more detailed information about the essential functions of a position, please send an e-mail to diversity.inclusion_ch@novartis.com and let us know the nature of your request and your contact information. Please include the job requisition number in your message.

Job Description Summary

 
Job Description
El/la Portfolio & Life-Cycle Management Lead actuará como catalizador/a de decisiones estratégicas de negocio a lo largo del portfolio.
El rol evaluará de forma continua el desempeño del portfolio, la evolución del mercado y los principales hitos del ciclo de vida de los productos, con el objetivo de identificar oportunidades para acelerar el crecimiento, mejorar la rentabilidad, proteger el valor y mitigar riesgos. Transformará estos insights en recomendaciones claras, business cases sólidos y planes de acción ejecutables.
Asimismo, tendrá un papel clave en el desarrollo y consolidación de Portfolio & Life-Cycle Management como una capacidad estratégica en Novartis España, estableciendo marcos de toma de decisiones, mecanismos de gobernanza y formas de trabajo cross-functional que refuercen la priorización del portfolio y su ejecución.
No se trata de un rol tradicional de gestión de una única marca. Requiere una visión transversal del negocio y del portfolio, un sólido criterio empresarial y capacidad para influir en decisiones entre diferentes funciones y áreas terapéuticas, sin necesidad de autoridad formal.
Responsabilidades clave 
Estrategia de portfolio e identificación de oportunidades 
Realizar revisiones de portfolio proactivas y continuas para identificar oportunidades de crecimiento, protección del valor, eficiencia y mitigación de riesgos. 
Evaluar el rendimiento, el potencial futuro y la relevancia estratégica de las marcas en distintas etapas de su ciclo de vida. 
Traducir los insights del portfolio en prioridades estratégicas claras y recomendaciones de negocio accionables. 
Evaluar y priorizar oportunidades en función de su impacto potencial, viabilidad, nivel de inversión, retorno esperado y riesgos asociados. 
Desarrollar business cases, evaluaciones financieras y escenarios que respalden las decisiones de asignación de recursos e inversión. 
Monitorizar la implementación y el impacto en el negocio de las iniciativas de portfolio priorizadas. 
Gestión del ciclo de vida y preparación para la LoE 
Anticipar los hitos críticos del ciclo de vida de los productos, incluida la pérdida de exclusividad (LoE), los cambios en la dinámica de mercado y los cambios en el entorno competitivo, regulatorio o de acceso. 
Desarrollar estrategias de ciclo de vida diferenciadas según la madurez, el rendimiento y la relevancia estratégica de cada marca. 
Elaborar planes estructurados de preparación para la LoE y de mitigación de riesgos, en colaboración con los equipos transversales pertinentes. 
Identificar y activar palancas de optimización del valor en áreas como pricing, estrategia de suministro, gestión de la demanda, mantenimiento de marca, simplificación del modelo operativo y asignación de recursos. 
Apoyar la transición de marcas a la Commercial Portfolio Unit, asegurando una transferencia efectiva del conocimiento de negocio, los insights de rendimiento, las responsabilidades y las prioridades estratégicas. 
Identificar oportunidades para simplificar, externalizar o racionalizar determinadas actividades o activos del portfolio cuando proceda. 
Liderazgo transversal y ejecución 
Liderar la evaluación, priorización y activación de iniciativas transversales de portfolio. 
Reunir a Marketing, Market Access, Finanzas, Asuntos Regulatorios, Supply, Legal y otras funciones relevantes en torno a una base de datos y una recomendación comunes. 
Generar alineamiento entre stakeholders con objetivos, perspectivas e incentivos distintos. 
Cuestionar de forma constructiva los supuestos y las formas de trabajo existentes para encontrar mejores soluciones para el negocio. 
Presentar recomendaciones de portfolio, business cases y disyuntivas estratégicas a stakeholders sénior y foros de decisión. 
Asegurar que las prioridades acordadas se traduzcan en responsables claros, planes de implementación y mecanismos de seguimiento. 
Desarrollo de capacidades y transformación organizativa 
Contribuir a consolidar la Commercial Portfolio Unit como una capacidad estratégica de gestión de portfolio dentro de Novartis España. 
Diseñar e implantar marcos de gestión de portfolio, foros de gobierno, herramientas, procesos y criterios de decisión. 
Promover una cultura de creación de valor, priorización, simplificación y toma de decisiones basada en datos. 
Actuar como referente interno en Gestión de Portfolio y del Ciclo de Vida. 
Fomentar la colaboración y el intercambio de conocimiento entre áreas terapéuticas y funciones. 
Identificar oportunidades para reforzar las capacidades de gestión de portfolio mediante nuevos enfoques, analítica, tecnologías y formas de trabajo. 
Perfil del candidato 
Buscamos a un profesional con experiencia, sólida visión de negocio, criterio estratégico y capacidad para convertir la complejidad en decisiones y acción. 
La persona ideal será intelectualmente curiosa, con mentalidad comercial y cómoda cuestionando el statu quo. Más que exigir experiencia en un puesto concreto, buscamos a alguien capaz de identificar, priorizar y capturar oportunidades en un portfolio diverso. 
Formación 
Titulación universitaria en Ciencias de la Salud, Farmacia, Administración de Empresas, Economía, Ingeniería o una disciplina afín. 
Se valorará un MBA o un posgrado en Estrategia, Marketing, Finanzas o Dirección de Empresas. 
Experiencia profesional 
Aproximadamente 7–10 años de experiencia profesional relevante en la industria farmacéutica, biotecnológica o sanitaria, o en consultoría estratégica. 
Experiencia en una o varias funciones comerciales o estratégicas, como Marketing, Market Access, Ventas, Excelencia Comercial, Finanzas, Planificación Estratégica, Gestión de Portfolio o Gestión del Ciclo de Vida. 
Exposición a marcas en distintas etapas de su ciclo de vida, incluidas marcas maduras y productos próximos a la pérdida de exclusividad (LoE). 
Experiencia en la evaluación de oportunidades de negocio, el desarrollo de business cases y el apoyo a decisiones de inversión o de asignación de recursos. 
Capacidad demostrada para liderar iniciativas complejas y transversales en organizaciones matriciales. 
Experiencia trabajando con stakeholders sénior e influyendo en decisiones sin autoridad formal. 
Se valorará la experiencia en transiciones de productos farmacéuticos, estrategias de final de ciclo de vida o preparación de la LoE, aunque no es imprescindible si la persona candidata demuestra sólidas capacidades estratégicas y comerciales. 
Capacidades clave 
Capacidades técnicas y de negocio 
Gestión estratégica del portfolio y del ciclo de vida de los productos. 
Identificación, evaluación y dimensionamiento de oportunidades. 
Desarrollo de business cases y evaluación financiera. 
Modelización de escenarios y evaluación de riesgos. 
Análisis de mercado, de clientes y de la competencia. 
Priorización del portfolio y decisiones de asignación de recursos. 
Interpretación de datos comerciales y financieros. 
Liderazgo de programas y proyectos transversales. 
Traducción de insights en recomendaciones de negocio accionables. 
Capacidades de liderazgo y mentalidad 
Pensamiento estratégico y sólido criterio de negocio. 
Capacidad para conectar la visión global del portfolio con acciones de negocio concretas. 
Sólidas capacidades analíticas y capacidad para tomar decisiones con información incompleta. 
Pensamiento crítico y confianza para cuestionar de forma constructiva los supuestos establecidos. 
Capacidad para influir, generar alineamiento e impulsar avances sin autoridad formal. 
Comunicación clara y convincente, con habilidades de storytelling. 
Sólidas capacidades de gestión de stakeholders. 
Pragmatismo, responsabilidad y una fuerte orientación a la ejecución. 
Curiosidad intelectual y apertura a nuevos enfoques y tecnologías. 
Capacidad para desenvolverse en la ambigüedad y crear estructura, prioridades y planes de acción. 
Mentalidad corporativa, con capacidad para priori

Today, Lonza is a global leader in life sciences operating across three continents. While we work in science, there’s no magic formula to how we do it. Our greatest scientific solution is talented people working together, devising ideas that help businesses to help people. In exchange, we let our people own their careers. Their ideas, big and small, genuinely improve the world. And that’s the kind of work we want to be part of.
 
As Director / Senior Director, Strategic CAPEX & Investment Portfolio Management, you will shape investment decisions across Lonza’s Specialized Modalities platform. You will lead investment governance, capital planning and portfolio prioritization, helping translate business needs into strategically aligned, financially robust investment proposals.
Working closely with sites, Operations, Commercial Development, Engineering, Finance and Global Value Assurance, you will guide investments from initial opportunity assessment through approval and mobilization. You will also maintain portfolio-level oversight through delivery and value realization, ensuring insights inform future capital allocation decisions.

https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/benchling/f8f82.description:
We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.

When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.

Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.

We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today.






ROLE OVERVIEW

Benchling is building a world-class Professional Services team to drive implementations for our rapidly expanding customer base. Implementation Managers work with our customers, from small Biotech startups to the largest BioPharmas in the world to develop a deep understanding of their R&D Processes, and roll out solutions that transform how their research teams work together.



To be successful in this role, you will leverage your scientific background, project management skills, and product expertise to drive successful implementations of the Benchling platform. You will work hand in hand with the research scientists at our customers, and teams throughout Benchling to implement our solutions, and ensure our customers are successful. Implementation Managers lead all aspects of customer rollouts from requirements analysis and solution design, to configurations, testing, training, and onboarding users onto the system.  Fluent or native French or German, plus experience supporting French- or German-speaking customers.

 


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Manage initial rollouts for new Benchling customers as well as expansion projects with new teams or for new processes at existing customers

 - Own implementation success from project kickoff to go-live, leveraging strong project management skills, scientific expertise, and deep product knowledge.

 - Build and execute detailed project plans, own project activities, work with other team members to execute on project deliverables to ensure on time, on budget, high quality deployments.

 - Understand customers' scientific workflows and determine how Benchling can best be leveraged to meet their key business needs.

 - Lead requirements and design workshops, perform data modeling & application configuration, develop test plans and guide UAT execution, train and onboard users.

 - Act as a trusted advisor for customers, guiding them through the implementation ensuring they leverage and apply Benchling Best Practices.

 - Understand and document customer pain points, advocate for them internally to influence product changes.

 - Identify and work with sales on opportunities for account expansion post go-live.

 


QUALIFICATIONS

 - MS or Ph.D. in Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Immunology, Bioinformatics, Biological Engineering or a related field.

 - At least 2 years of experience in a lab or R&D setting, ideally in antibody discovery or strain engineering or process development. You must be able to empathize with scientists and quickly understand complicated scientific concepts.

 - Software Implementation experience, preferably with a SaaS software company.

 - Strong communication skills. You must be able to quickly and effectively connect with a range of stakeholders, including scientists, IT project leads, and executives.

 - Self-starter with the ability to be successful in a startup environment.

 - Curious, creative, and tenacious. You should be excited to collaborate with customers and other Benchling teammates as a thought partner.

 - Ability to travel up to 25% based on customer and project needs.

 - Fluent or native proficiency in French or German

 - Experience using Benchling, especially if you’ve been a Benchling administrator, is preferred but not required.

 


HOW WE WORK

We offer a flexible hybrid work arrangement that prioritizes in-office collaboration. Employees are expected to be on-site 3 days per week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday).




#LI-Hybrid 

#BI-Hybrid 

Benchling welcomes everyone.

We believe diversity enriches our team so we hire people with a wide range of identities, backgrounds, and experiences. 

We are an equal opportunity employer. That means we don’t discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We also consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law, including but not limited to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

Introduction
Help shape the future of healthcare AI, where innovation meets trust.
At CERN, you will develop cutting-edge AI solutions that help prevent disease, improve prediction, and deliver trustworthy healthcare insights. You will work on technologies that make it possible to unlock the value of sensitive data without ever moving or exposing it, enabling collaboration where privacy is essential.
As part of this role, you will help develop and deploy CAFEIN®, CERN's federated AI platform powering major European healthcare initiatives, including UMBRELLA and AIM-SAFE. You will design advanced federated learning algorithms and secure distributed AI systems that allow models to learn from data across institutions while keeping the data exactly where it belongs.
Recognised as a lighthouse example of "data stays, AI collaborates", CAFEIN® combines state-of-the-art federated learning with CERN's unique strengths in trust, open science, GDPR compliance, and international collaboration. The result is a pioneering framework that is redefining how AI can advance healthcare while safeguarding privacy.
Join us to build AI that learns globally, protects locally, and improves lives.
Functions
Develop and test federated learning software and algorithms.
Implement and evaluate privacy-preserving techniques, including differential privacy and homomorphic encryption.
Develop tools to optimise data ingestions and assess the quality of data and images. 
Design and run machine-learning experiments using programming languages like Python with libraries as TensorFLow, PyTorch, or scikit-learn. 
Analyse data using statistical methods and visualisation for exploratory data analysis (EDA). 
Implement and benchmark state-of-the-art machine-learning methods, optimising federated learning for utility, communication efficiency, energy use and scalability. 
Design and deploy Internet of Things (IoT)-based federated learning architectures.

At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position
We are seeking a Patent Attorney Trainee with a biochemistry / biomedical background. As a member of our group responsible for Large Molecule pharmaceutical products (biologicals) you will advise our scientists on the patenting of inventions in this field. On your path to develop as European Patent Attorney, you will secure patent protection, freedom to operate and market exclusivity during the life cycle of Roche´s products in close collaboration with the members of all functions involved.

The opportunity:

Handling of invention reports and drafting of patent applications in close collaboration with Research & Development
Handling of patent aspects for Large Molecule projects and products, including prosecution, defense and enforcement of patent rights
Patent portfolio management, supporting the decision making process for worldwide filings, maintenance and abandonment of patent filings
Performing freedom to operate analysis
Review of planned publications
Evaluation of contract terms related to IP and coordination with the Legal and Licensing departments on the drafting and negotiating of same
Preparation for the European Qualification Examination under supervision of an experienced patent attorney

Who you are:

Biochemistry / biomedical (or related) background, at least with a master degree, and a strong and broadly based interest in science and technology
Strong interest in patent law and interdisciplinary matters with a will to broaden horizons in this field and taking pleasure in a variety of intellectually stimulating work
Ideally, 1 to 2 years experience as a Trainee Patent Attorney in a Patent Law firm or equivalent
English language skills; knowledge of additional languages, in particular German, will be an advantage
Well-developed analytical and writing skills
Finely honed interpersonal skills and collaborative mindset
Ability to work to tight deadlines and to handle several projects simultaneously
Well-structured, reliable and precise style of work
Strong business acumen and interest in the pharmaceutical industry
 
 

Who we are
A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.

Let’s build a healthier future, together.

Roche is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Electronics testing and development support.
Software development support.

Experience in the design of PCBs, their production and verification/debugging.
Experience in programming microcontrollers.
Hands-on experience in soldering and handling of electrical equipment.
Experience in writing technical reports, user documentation and manuals.
Skills:
PCB design software, preferably Altium or KiCad.
Programming in C/C++ and Python.
Ability to operate multimeters, oscilloscopes and a VNA.
Demonstrating flexibility: adapting quickly and resourcefully to shifting priorities and requirements.

Working in a mixed team of engineers, technicians and physicists.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.

The actual location of this job is in VISP, Switzerland. Relocation assistance is available for eligible candidates and their families, if needed. 

Today, Lonza is a global leader in life sciences operating across five continents. While we work in science, there’s no magic formula to how we do it. Our greatest scientific solution is talented people working together, devising ideas that help businesses to help people. In exchange, we let our people own their careers. Their ideas, big and small, genuinely improve the world. And that’s the kind of work we want to be part of.
Join Lonza AG's Microbiology Quality Control team in Visp, Switzerland as a Scientist and contribute to our success in life sciences.
 
 
What you’ll get:
An agile career and dynamic working culture
An inclusive and ethical workplace
Compensation programs that recognize high performance
Along with competitive salaries, you’ll find a wide range of lifestyle, family and leisure benefits available. Depending on your location, these benefits could include family allowances, childcare support, discounts for local businesses and attractions, travel allowances, and subsidized meals.
 
 
What you'll do:
Represent the QC Microbiology department at internal and customer meetings, audits, and inspections for assigned projects.
Scientific SME for project-specific analyses and other microbial analyses in QC Microbiology: Monitoring, evaluating, and, if necessary, coordinating the implementation of current improvements.
Coordinate completion of work packages within business units, ensuring timely communication among interdisciplinary teams.
Collection, investigation, and evaluation of verification data, identifying weak points, and implementing corrective measures to ensure flawless operations. Defining cGMP examinations in the event of deviations, ensuring compliance and maintaining our proven track record of excellence.
Participation in the creation and release of technical documentation, including the development of verification plans and reports. Development and verification of analytical microbiology methods to uphold our strict standards of quality.
Supporting other departments with Quality Assurance tasks and contributing to various projects at the Visp site team. Driving process improvements to maintain our competitive edge.
Readiness for on-call duty approximately 3-4 times per year, with assignments carried out from home.
 
 
What we are looking for:
MSc or PhD in Microbiology, Biology, or Pharmaceutical Sciences, or equivalent experience.
Proven work experience in pharmaceutical Quality Control, particularly with endotoxin and/or bioburden analysis is highly desirable.
GMP knowledge is highly desirable.
You stay organized and manage to keep an overview of many tasks even when times are very busy. You enjoy being in contact with many different internal and external partners.
Proficiency in English is essential; German language skills are advantageous.
 
This is an outstanding opportunity to join a team where your expertise will be valued, and your contributions will have a significant impact!

/job/Basel/Compound-Logistics-Workflow-a.description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position
At Roche, we believe it’s urgent to deliver medical solutions right now – even as we develop innovations for the future. We are passionate about transforming patients’ lives and we are fearless in both decision and action. And we believe that good business means a better world. That is why we come to work each day. We commit ourselves to scientific rigor, unassailable ethics, and access to medical innovations for all. We do this today to build a better tomorrow.

In the Small Molecule Research department (SMR) in Pharma Research and Early Development (pRED), we generate molecular insights, and drive the discovery and development of small molecules from initial starting points to clinical candidates across the pRED discovery portfolio. In the Compound Library Enhancement and Logistics (CLEL) team, we supply research samples for all SMR portfolio projects and serve as the custodians of the Roche Corporate Compound Collection. Using state-of-the-art automation platforms and digital workflows, our mission is to enable drug discovery projects with the supply of proprietary chemical space and the timely delivery of research samples that can be subjected to biological assays. 

As the CLEL team is spearheading novel digital processes and AI-augmented drug discovery workflows, we are seeking an analytical and forward-thinking scientist to join our team in the Roche Innovation Center Basel and contribute to the exploration and implementation of next-generation end-to-end sample logistics workflows. 

The position:
In this role, you will focus on building the next-generation workflow engines that track, plan, and securely connect decisions across our entire automated IT infrastructure. You will serve as a key business analyst, modernizing legacy systems, eliminating static steps, and replacing them with fully automated, FAIR-compliant, interoperable workflows and data foundations built for scalable automation and AI that keep the drug discovery path moving at maximum velocity.
This role will deliver efficiency gains by lowering business process overhead and improve coordination. It will also increase visibility and develop new planning capabilities leading to better decisions on investments and strategic resource planning, resulting in streamlined sample delivery and data processes.
Specifically, you will:
Scope, design and engineer an interconnected next-generation business workflow engine capable of mapping, tracking, and capturing decisions and data across automated business processes.
Develop solutions to lower technical barriers for sample, data and information transfer, as well as decision-making at the interface of internal or external stakeholder-facing systems.
Support compliance workflows in sample and data management (i.e. sample decisions, documentation), as well as overhaul automated compound QC workflows towards AI-assisted data analysis pipelines.
Partner with automation engineers and laboratory staff to generate business dashboards and track key performance indicators (KPIs) and interface effectiveness to key stakeholders.
Shape and drive our ongoing transition to AI-based software development: build and maintain tools together with AI coding assistants, and establish the practices (review, testing, documentation) that keep AI-generated solutions reliable and future-oriented.
Design and implement agentic workflows in which AI agents carry out multi-step tasks such as data analysis, issue diagnosis and routine operations, with clear human oversight and safeguards for operational systems and data.
Act as expert point of contact for operational workflows: shape the evolution of our system landscape, develop solutions with emerging AI technologies, and contribute to the architecture of future tools.

Who you are:
You’re someone who wants to influence your own development. You’re looking to be part of a dynamic and cutting-edge organization where you have the opportunity to pursue your interests across functions and tasks. You are interested in making an impact by providing solutions, reducing complexity and connecting essential elements of the drug discovery process and are passionate about applying state-of-the-art technology and science to the biopharmaceutical industry.

You have a university degree, preferably an M.S. or B.S. in computer science, cheminformatics, a life science or another scientific discipline with a strong computational focus, or show equivalent practical experience and expertise in laboratory automation and research informatics.
You have exceptionally structured thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to bridge physical logistics with software logic. You can also translate complex thoughts into practical, robust, applications and solutions.
You have a solid experience in Business Analysis (BA), process mapping, or operations engineering, specifically within a pharmaceutical or biotechnology research facility.
You must be familiar with laboratory information flows, sample management logistics, and automated compound QC workflows.
You are comfortable working with and taking ownership of software-based solutions, from Python, SQL and relational databases to version-controlled codebases, testing, deployment and operation in server-based environments.
You have hands-on experience with agentic AI tools (e.g. Claude Code, GitHub Copilot) used for real work beyond chat: handing over multi-step tasks, giving AI agents the right context, and critically verifying what they produce.
You have strong interpersonal skills to influence, advise and collaborate with experts, vendors and IT partners in a matrix environment to jointly move projects forward.
Your profile is rounded off by having good presentation and communication skills in English.

The scientific title of this position might be adjusted depending on the experience and seniority of the final candidate.
If you are proud of contributing and feel you have the dedication to teamwork and innovation that we are seeking, then Roche is the organization for you. Every role at Roche plays a part in making a difference to patients’ lives. If you want to work in a passionate team, make your mark and improve lives, apply now.

 
 

Who we are
A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.

Let’s build a healthier future, together.

Roche is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Vos responsabilités principales sont les suivantes :Pour mener à bien cette mission, nous recherchons une personne ayant le profil suivant :

Réviser et approuver les dossiers de lots, protocoles de fabrication, rapports de qualification / validation, programmes de maintenance / étalonnage et autres documents qualité associés

Préparer les protocoles de libération

Assurer un support qualité dans la gestion des événements qualité (déviations, investigations, CAPA et demandes de changement) et contribuer à leur résolution

Veiller au respect des exigences réglementaires et la conformité des procédés conformément aux BPF, aux AMM et aux SOP et aux dossiers de validation

Contribuer à la préparation et au déroulement des audits, inspections et visites réglementaires

Participer à l'amélioration continue des systèmes qualité et de la documentation du site

Développer une présence terrain active afin de promouvoir la culture qualité et accompagner les équipes opérationnelles

Participer aux projets qualité transverses, au suivi des indicateurs de performance et à la formation des collaborateurs sur les bonnes pratiques GxP

Pour mener à bien cette mission, nous recherchons une personne ayant le profil suivant :

Formation supérieure en Pharmacie, Biologie, Biochimie, Chimie ou domaine équivalent

Au minimum 2 à 3 ans d'expérience dans l'industrie pharmaceutique ou biotechnologique dans un rôle lié à la qualité ou la production ; bonnes connaissances de processus de fabrication un réel atout

Solides connaissances des BPF, avec une bonne compréhension des systèmes qualité pharmaceutiques

Maîtrise de la Suite Ms Office et des systèmes ERP (idéalement Sage X3) ; expérience avec les outils Trackwise / EDMS / LMS valorisée

Excellente maîtrise du français, à l’oral comme à l’écrit ; anglais apprécié

Vous vous décrivez comme une personne rigoureuse, proactive et orientée solutions. Cette opportunité vous intéresse ? Transmettez-nous au plus vite votre candidature et rejoignez les équipes d'OM Pharma !

 

 
About Us

OM Pharma is a global Geneva-based biopharmaceutical company. It is a leader in the prevention of recurrent respiratory and urinary tract infections and is also active in the treatment of vascular diseases.

It operates worldwide through a strong network of international partners and invests its profits in R&D to develop microbial derived immunotherapeutic products to treat acute and chronic immunological disorders resulting from inflammation and infections. 

The company strives to improve the quality of life of patients around the world by providing access to better treatment of immunological imbalances.

For more information, visit the website: ompharma.com.
