MEDICAL ADVISOR

CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES | SWITZERLAND | 100% | 12-MONTH FIXED-TERM CONTRACT

To strengthen our Medical and Patient Affairs team in Geneva, we are looking for a Medical Advisor Cardiovascular Diseases. You will help shape and execute the local medical strategy, build trusted scientific partnerships and translate medical insights into initiatives that improve patient outcomes in Switzerland.

 

Who we are

Servier (Suisse) S.A. is the Swiss affiliate of Servier, an independent international pharmaceutical group governed by a foundation. With its governance model, the Group is committed to therapeutic progress to serve patients and integrates the patient voice at every stage of the medicine life cycle. As a leading global player in cardiology and venous diseases, Servier aims to become a leading innovator in oncology and neurology. The Group intends to offer targeted therapeutic solutions, particularly in rare cancers and neurological diseases, and invests nearly 20% of its brand-name sales in R&D. Headquartered in France, Servier relies on its more than 20,000 employees and a solid geographic presence with medicines distributed in more than 130 countries. As Servier employees, we are united by shared values and guided by a common vision. Together, we share an entrepreneurial spirit and are committed to advancing therapeutic progress to address patients’ unmet needs.

 
Your role

As Medical Advisor Cardiovascular Diseases, you will report to the Medical and Patient Affairs Manager and collaborate closely with Commercial, Marketing, Market Access, Regulatory Affairs, Pharmacovigilance and Global Medical and Patient Affairs teams. You will provide medical leadership to internal and external stakeholders, support evidence generation and scientific communication, and contribute to the development and implementation of the local medical strategy throughout the product lifecycle.

 

As Medical Advisor Cardiovascular Diseases, you will

SHAPE

Contribute to the development and execution of the local medical strategy for cardiovascular diseases.

Identify unmet medical needs, treatment trends and evidence gaps, and translate insights into impactful medical initiatives.

Provide strategic medical input to lifecycle management, brand planning and cross-functional projects.

Monitor emerging scientific evidence, clinical-practice developments, congress highlights and relevant publications within the therapeutic area.

 

ENGAGE

Build and maintain trusted scientific partnerships with healthcare professionals, therapeutic-area experts, scientific societies, patient organizations and other relevant stakeholders.

Develop and maintain a comprehensive understanding of the healthcare ecosystem, including key healthcare professionals, centres, networks, multidisciplinary teams, referral pathways and other relevant stakeholders..

Organise advisory boards, scientific exchanges and educational initiatives while gathering and communicating actionable medical insights.

Develop and deliver medical training and scientific updates for cross-functional teams, contributing to onboarding and continuous learning initiatives.

 

DELIVER

Deliver accurate, balanced and compliant scientific information to internal and external stakeholders, and contribute to the development, review and validation of scientific and educational materials.

Support local evidence-generation activities, including real-world evidence projects, registries, observational studies, investigator-initiated trials, scientific publications and congress activities.

Provide medical leadership and scientific guidance for affiliate projects and cross-functional initiatives.

Monitor and communicate medical activities, stakeholder engagement, project outcomes, risks and opportunities through appropriate reporting.

Ensure all activities comply with applicable regulatory, legal, ethical and pharmacovigilance standards.

 

What you bring

Advanced university degree in a health-related scientific discipline, such as MD, PharmD, PhD, MSc or equivalent.

Relevant experience in Medical Affairs and/or Patient Affairs within the pharmaceutical industry.

Experience in medical strategy development, scientific communication, medical review, evidence generation or clinical-research projects.

Strong project-management skills and the ability to manage several activities simultaneously.

Fluency in English; good command of French and/or German is strongly preferred.

Strong digital literacy, including the use of insight-generation, AI and project-management tools.

 

How you work

You communicate complex scientific and medical information clearly and effectively to different audiences.

You build trusted scientific relationships and collaborate effectively across functions and with external stakeholders.

You influence and create alignment without direct authority, while working both autonomously and collaboratively.

You bring learning agility, curiosity, resilience and adaptability to a dynamic environment.

You combine strong business acumen with a focus on patient value and organisational priorities.

You are committed to partnering with patients and patient communities and to integrating patient perspectives into medical activities and decision-making.

 

Additional assets

Experience in arterial hypertension and heart failure.

Experience with real-world evidence, registries, observational studies, investigator-initiated trials or scientific publications.

Familiarity with the Swiss pharmaceutical environment, healthcare system and relevant cardiovascular stakeholder networks.

Experience collaborating with scientific societies, therapeutic-area experts and multidisciplinary healthcare teams.

 

What we offer

The opportunity to help shape cardiovascular medical strategy in Switzerland.

A collaborative environment with direct exposure to local and international stakeholders.

Flexible ways of working, combining home office and presence in a modern workplace in Geneva.

Ongoing learning and opportunities for personal and professional development.

A competitive compensation package and a supportive team culture.

 
Join Servier and contribute to a purpose-driven company committed to therapeutic progress for the benefit of patients. We value diversity, inclusion, and equal opportunities, and we welcome applications from all qualified candidates. At Servier, we believe that our differences make us stronger and that every talent deserves the opportunity to grow and make an impact.

The Electrical Engineering Group (EN-EL) at CERN is responsible for the electrical power-distribution network (from 400 kV to 400/230V), for the fibre-optics infrastructure, and for signal and DC-power cabling for the accelerator complex.
You will join the electrical Design and Documentation Office (EN-EL-DDO). You will take on a support electrical designer role. This will include the creation and modification of electrical drawings, design of low voltage distribution networks, cable sizing, equipment sizing, LV protection studies and the general support to senior electrical designers. With time you will be required to take on design tasks of increasing complexity. In addition, you will oversee various quality-related activities within the Design Office, such as the management of the printing office and the maintenance and updating of templates.
This is the perfect opportunity for a junior technician to further establish their existing knowledge of low voltage distribution circuits by putting it into practice.
Your responsibilities:
Preparing design drawings using CAD software.
Preparing calculation notes using ElecCalc/Caneco BT or similar.
Preparing bills of material and cabling tables for electrical-related equipment in Excel.
Updating excel based design templates.
General quality related tasks in the design office.
Your profile:
Demonstrated experience in:
The design of Low voltage distribution networks, cable sizing and selectivity studies.
Producing drawings in AutoCAD or similar.
The intermediate level of Microsoft EXCEL.
Skills:
An understanding of low voltage distribution networks (selectivity, completing calculation notes, knowledge of European LV standards, protection, protection of circuits for indirect contact, knowledge of different types of earthing systems).
An understanding of power systems; voltage drop calculations, short circuit calculations, understanding fault levels, dimensioning of cables.
Experience on low voltage design calculation tools (ElecCalc, Caneco or similar software).
Proficient in AutoCAD or similar.
Proficient in Microsoft Excel.
Spoken and written English or French, with a commitment to learn the basics of the other language.
Beneficial skills/or knowledge:
Experience on the design of lighting systems for buildings and external areas using DIALux.
Experience with E-PLAN or similar software.
Experience in the design of medium voltage distribution networks.
Motivated candidates without direct design office experience would still be considered.

By the application deadline, you have a maximum of two years of professional experience since graduation in Electrical Engineering (or a related field) and your highest educational qualification is a general secondary education diploma.
You have never had a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.
Applicants with a Bachelor's, Master's or PhD degree are not eligible.

The successful candidate will join an innovative Antibody Discovery and Engineering department with a strong record of success in developing novel antibody therapeutics in the field of immune-oncology and autoimmune diseases. Design and develop novel naïve antibody and VHH libraries.

Lead and execute antibody discovery campaigns using phage, yeast, and mammalian display platforms.

Effectively support discovery programs and deliver project objectives within established timelines.

Demonstrated hands-on expertise in antibody engineering and lead discovery using display technologies, including phage, yeast, and/or mammalian display platforms.

Strong knowledge of molecular biology techniques, antibody expression systems, and biophysical characterization methods.

Experience with protein-protein interaction technologies and affinity characterization platforms, such as Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) and/or Bio-Layer Interferometry (BLI), is highly desirable.

Proven understanding of antibody discovery workflows, from library design and screening through candidate characterization and optimization.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to effectively communicate complex scientific concepts, influence stakeholders, and present research findings to diverse audiences at all levels of the organization.

Proactive, adaptable, and results-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic research environment.

Job Description

We are a research-driven biopharmaceutical company. Our mission is built on the simple premise that if we “follow the science” and that great medicines can make a significant impact to our world. And we believe that a research-driven enterprise dedicated to world-class science can succeed by inventing medicine and vaccine innovations that make a difference for patients across the globe.
 
You will be part of the BARDS organization which has a presence in the US, EU and Asia Pacific. By joining our company, in this role you will apply your skills and experience in support of developing scientifically based arguments aiming to provide fair accessibility to drugs and vaccines making a real difference in patient’s lives.
 
The Biostatistics and Research Decision Sciences (BARDS) organization has a proud record of providing comprehensive analytical and methodological expertise to support our company’s strategic goals.  Our quantitative scientists aspire to maintain the highest quality output while adopting the most efficient and effective scientific and operational procedures that will promote breakthrough innovation, collaboration and professional activity.
 
We are currently looking for a Biostatistician, HTA Statistics to join the team based in one of our offices in Zurich, Switzerland, Brussels, Belgium or London, UK.
 
The BARDS organization has established in Europe its Centre of Excellence supporting Health Technology Assessment (HTA) dossiers with presence in Brussels (Belgium), London (United Kingdom) and Zürich (Switzerland).  Our statisticians and statistical programmers collaborate with multiple functional areas across the company and with our local affiliates to ensure that the clinical trial data representing our products is characterized properly in these dossiers, and to develop innovative statistical approaches to novel problems in the HTA space. 
 
The primary activities include but are not limited to:
o   Provide statistical support to projects in the BARDS HTA Statistics group, including HTA submissions.
o   Contribute to the design and development of scientific tools for HTA evaluations.
o   Execute on ongoing HTA evaluations, including analysis and interpretation of HTA results.
o   Collaborate with Statistical Programming to implement methodologies and ensure high quality deliverables for HTA submissions.
o   Contribute to the preparation of the written reports to effectively communicate results of HTA evaluations to the Value & Implementation Observational Research (VIOR) and our company’s subsidiary teams.
o   May evaluate appropriateness of available software for planned analyses and ascertains needs for potential program development of novel statistical methodology.
o   May be involved in research activities for innovative statistical methods and applications in HTA activities.
 
Qualifications:
Education and Minimum Requirement: 
o   Master`s or bachelor’s degree in statistics/biostatistics or a related discipline
 
Required Skills and Experience:
o   Fluency in English (oral and written).
o   Good knowledge of biostatistical methodologies and experimental design, including meta-analyses and time-to-event methodologies. 
o   Proven knowledge of statistical and data processing software in R. 
o   Demonstrates strong interest in statistical research activities and in application of novel methods to clinical development. 
o   Team oriented, strong collaboration skills and ability to work effectively across cultures.  
o   Must also demonstrate the ability to learn, be proactive and motivated, and consistently focus on details and execution.
 
Preferred Skills and Experience:
o   Understanding of data management and clinical concepts applied to drug development within the pharmaceutical industry.
o   Strong knowledge of computer systems and clinical databases systems in a statistical environment.
o   Experience in CDISC data standards (SDTM, ADAM)
o   Proven knowledge of statistical and data processing software in SAS.
o   Understanding of biology of disease and drug development.  
o   Publication record in peer reviewed statistical/medical journals
 
Our Quantitative Sciences team use big data to analyse the safety and efficacy claims of our potential medical breakthroughs. We review the quality and reliability of clinical studies using deep scientific knowledge, statistical analysis and high-quality data to support decision making in clinical trials.

Job Description

We have an exciting new opportunity for a Principal Scientist to join our Health Economics and Decision Sciences group in Switzerland and focus on health economic modeling for Oncology products, offering the opportunity to add meaningful scientific and patient impact.

Hybrid and flexible work arrangements are possible, consistent with local office and country policies.

About the Department

The Health Economics and Decision Sciences (HEDS) department is part of our company’s Biostatistics and Research Decision Sciences (BARDS) organization.
BARDS is responsible for strategic design and analysis to enable informed decision making in the discovery, development, and delivery of our company’s innovative products, and is a leader in quantitative scientific methodology and its application to enable the targeting, discovery, development, manufacturing, and marketing of drugs and vaccines for the benefit of patients and global public health.
In collaboration with internal and external partners, the BARDS-HEDS department specifically provides strategic and technical leadership to enable patient access, measure and quantify the value of our company’s products, inform internal and external decisions, and shape methodology and external health policy and practice.
This position will focus on health economic modeling for oncology products.

What you will do:

You will report to the HEDS Senior Director and provide strategic development and use of industry-leading predictive and economic models to enhance our understanding of disease and to quantify and communicate the value of our Oncology products to patients, providers, and payers.
Serve as the BARDS HEDS lead for one or more Value and Implementation teams to develop health economic, disease, and predictive models to enable business insights for the product.
Utilize discovery, real world evidence, clinical trial and published data, and publicly available information and tools to provide economic and integrated models to answer key questions in all phases of drug and vaccine development – Phase I through loss of data exclusivity.
Advance the use of integrated quantitative approaches, focusing on economic, disease, and predictive modeling and simulation in partnership with other internal groups and external organizations.
Development and maintenance of health quality global health economic models and tools in-house or in collaboration with external vendors to provide critical business insights and fully demonstrate the value of our company’s products.
Support and training of HEDS models and tools to support country/regional team adaptations and communications with external stakeholders.
Dissemination of health economic data via presentations at congresses and publications in scientific journals.
Work closely with external collaborators (clinical/economic thought leaders, payer/HTA experts, alliance partners) and internal cross-functional teams to ensure that new methodologies, models, and advanced analytics are fully utilized for our products.
Maintain awareness of external data, modeling methodologies and IT tools to collaborate across relevant internal stakeholders to enhance the company capabilities in health economic modeling, simulation, and data visualization.  
Ensure sharing of work product and relevant best practices across the enterprise.

Education

PhD (preferred) or Master’s degree, in Health Economics, Biostatistics, Health Services Research, Actuarial Sciences, Operations Research or a closely related, quantitative field

Required Experience and Skills:

Relevant work experience in health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) of 5 or more years beyond PhD (or 7 or more years beyond Master’s degree)
Knowledge and experience in the economic evaluation of Oncology drugs and interventions
Expertise and solid hands-on experience in the conceptualization, design, development and dissemination of health economic model approaches to enable internal and external decisions
Track record of submissions to Health Technology Assessment bodies and research publications in conferences and peer-reviewed journals
Understanding of the market access environment and challenges in the US and key international markets

Competencies/Skills:

Leadership skills, with experience in managing resources and driving implementation
Strong interpersonal, organizational and communication skills with ability to interact with individuals from a variety of disciplines
Eye for detail
Collaborative approach

Closing date for applications: 7th December 2026

Job Description

We are seeking an exceptional leader to serve as Vice President, Regulatory Affairs – CMC Large Molecule and Device Quality & Regulatory, the single point of executive accountability for large molecule Regulatory CMC including Biologics, Vaccines, and devices/ combination products. 

This position reports to the Senior Vice President, Regulatory, Chemistry, Manufacturing and Control (CMC) and Quality Assurance.    

This role in Research and Development (R&D) operates at the critical intersection of Development, Manufacturing Operations, Science & Technology, Quality, and Supply Chain Management, this executive establishes the regulatory vision and governs end-to-end execution across all development phases from First-in-Human clinical trials through commercial registrations (BLA, MAA, J-NDA).  The role is also accountable for lifecycle management for large molecules and combination products.

Leading a multi-site organization of approximately 200 to 300 regulatory scientists and device quality professionals the Vice President ensures that enterprise pipeline programs spanning monoclonal antibodies, bi-specifics, antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), vaccines, and device / combination products are advanced with regulatory sciences rigor, speed, and compliance across global commercial markets. 

Responsibilities could expand to other technical modalities as the pipeline continues to evolve. Direct reports for this role include Associate Vice Presidents for Biologics and New Modalities, Vaccines, and Devices Quality and Regulatory.
 
Key Responsibilities:

Strategic Leadership & Regulatory Accountability
Lead establishment of regulatory CMC strategies from clinical through commercial phases for large molecule (biologics and vaccines) and new modalities including monoclonal antibodies, bispecifics, ADCs, and vaccines.   
Ensure integration of high quality scientific content and control strategies into regulatory filings to enable process robustness and life cycle maintenance.
Provide leadership and direction for end-to-end global regulatory strategies and quality compliance for drug-device combination products, ensuring compliance with FDA and EU Regulations for autoinjectors, pre-filled syringes, and on-body delivery systems.
Lead oversight for the authoring and delivery of Common Technical Document (CTD) Module 3 and Module 2.3 Quality Overall Summaries across IND, CTA, BLA, MAA, and post-approval filings.
Partner with Regulatory CMC leadership to support the modernization of regulatory CMC workflows through structured data, component authoring and advanced digital tools.

Health Authority Interactions & Inspection Readiness
Ensure effective preparation and engage in Health Authority interactions, and meetings with major regulatory agencies (FDA CDER/CBER, EMA,) while representing the company externally to shape regulatory expectations.
Lead or sponsor utilization of advanced regulatory working groups (such as the FDA Emerging Technology Program and EMA Innovation Task Force) to build early consensus on novel manufacturing and analytical methods.
Partner with senior Quality leaders on inspection readiness programs, leading the regulatory strategy to prepare for Pre-Approval Inspections (PAIs) and responding to regulatory requests during GMP inspections or audits.
Sponsor ensuring ISO certification and maintenance to enable effective combination product submissions, approvals and inspections. 

Team Building & Talent Development
Build, lead, and mentor a high-performing and inclusive regulatory CMC/ device regulatory and quality team of scientists, managers, and experts. 
Foster a culture of innovative thinking and scientific excellence.
Develop succession plans and talent pipelines aligned with organizational goals.
Promote collaboration, knowledge sharing, and continuous learning.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Management
Partner and ensure effective cross functional collaboration to deliver submissions and approvals with key groups in development (Drug Substance, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Analytical Sciences and Quality Assurance) and Manufacturing, Quality, and Global Supply Chain.
Serve as the primary regulatory partner for Large Molecule and Devices with cross functional leaders and ensure effective review of submissions by cross functional areas to gain alignment on strategy and content.
Collaborate with Device Engineering and Human Factors teams to ensure design verification, validation, risk management files, and clinical usability assessments are properly embedded into Module 3 and device master files.
Represent Regulatory CMC and Device Regulatory and Quality on key development and manufacturing governance forums and lead teams. 
Ensure effective regulatory CMC due diligence assessments, and integration plans for acquisitions, in-licensing and external co-development partnerships.
Ensure effective collaboration and integration with other areas of Global Regulatory Affairs and Clinical Safety to deliver on submissions and approvals.

Team and Organizational Resource Management
Manage resources effectively to ensure timely delivery of projects and submissions, while partnering with other leaders in Regulatory CMC to manage budgets and headcount targets. 
Oversee leaders and actively manage multiple regulatory submissions ensuring timely delivery, quality, and alignment with business priorities.
Sponsor and collaborate on continuous improvement initiatives across the Regulatory CMC and enterprise to enable effective and efficient utilization of resources to maximize speed to market. 
Sponsor continuous improvement of the operating model for regulatory CMC activities in the US and globally to enable efficient regulatory deliverables. 
 
Education:
Advanced degree (Ph.D.) in Pharmaceutics, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Biochemistry, or related discipline is highly preferred.

Experience in achieving successful outcomes through formal interactions (FDA and EMA) with major global regulatory agencies.

Demonstrated success leading large, multi site organizations across North America and / or Europe.

Excellent business acumen and decision making that demonstrates an ability to translate complex technical and regulatory challenges into pragmatic, risk-mitigated strategies that align with enterprise business objectives.
Commitment to talent development and building succession depth, championing inclusion, while fostering a culture of technical rigor and continuous learning.

Position Purpose:
The Manager, Regional Regulatory Lead (RRL) in Global Regulatory Strategy (GRS) is a member of the respective GRA GRS Therapeutic Area and contributes to the vision and goals of CSL as:
·       Regulatory leaders who leverage regional regulatory experience to actively contribute to an innovative, scientifically sound, global, integrated regulatory vision / strategies for assigned product/s with a patient centric-focus, leveraging regional commercial insights and applying prudent risk-taking to ensure timely delivery of successful regulatory outcomes. 
·       Effectively partner with assigned product/s Global Regulatory Affairs Strategy Team (GRAST) GRL plus other regional, labeling and CMC GRAST members to ensure ‘One GRA Voice’, appropriate inputs into risk assessment and decision making.  Ensures bi-directional communication with stationed region commercial operations and GRA.
·       With support, engaging with health authority (HA) in stationed country (FDA or EMA), maintaining productive relationship with HA contacts and driving positive regulatory outcomes with respective HA for assigned product/s in conjunction with GRL.  Contributes to product health authority interaction with support GRL or Regulatory TA Head.
·       Partner with GRAST members to achieve regulatory deliverables (including leading assigned tasks) while fostering individual accountability, ‘team spirit’, actively contribute and executing on decisions expeditiously resulting in positive regulatory outcomes.
 
 
Main Responsibilities and Accountabilities:
1. With support, accountable for assigned product relationship with a health authority (FDA or EMA), ensuring alignment with product GRL and as needed, support from Head, Regulatory TA if escalation is required.  May negotiate on behalf of CSL with health authority to achieve desired regulatory outcome.
2. Developing regional knowledge regarding health authority requirements, regulatory filing pathway / categories, processes and ways of working and thus, can provide relevant guidance / assessment to internal stakeholders (e.g. GRAST, GRL & Commercial) on means to address project challenges, leverage regulatory opportunities and advise on risk for developmental, new and marketed products.
3. Under the product GRL, supports regional regulatory activities as assigned, inclusive of potential to contribute to core document preparation (e.g. core briefing book, pediatric plans, etc.), product filing preparation activities (investigational, new and marketed) and health authority engagements.  Responsible for Module 1 documentation required for submission and supports response to health authority comments activities with guidance from GRL.
4. Actively contribute to the GRAST activities, strategy development, document reviews and competitive regulatory intelligence.  Ensures on-time execution of regulatory activities at the regional level, achieving positive regulatory outcomes.  Partners with GRL to develop internal communications and distributes GRAS communications to regional commercial stakeholders. Actively connects and maintains relationships with GRAST members, including GRAS Regions and Regulatory CMC.
5. Proactively fosters and promotes effective relationships across Global Regulatory Strategy. Updates and maintains applicable regulatory systems (e.g. Veeva) to ensure tracking and compliance deliverables.
6. Applies the CSL Leadership Capabilities – Build Bridges, Think Beyond, Unleash Outcomes, Ignite Agility, Inspire the Future and Cultivate Talent – to oneself. 

Position Qualifications and Experience Requirements:
 
Education:
 
A bachelor’s degree (four-year university degree) in pharmacy, biology, chemistry, pharmacology, clinical medicine or related life science is required.  An advanced degree in a related field (MS, PhD or MD, DVM) or MBA is preferred.
 
Experience:
 
Minimum of 5 years’ experience in the biotech or pharmaceutical industry, with exposure to regulatory activities / submissions and 3 years working on developmental products. Previous regulatory affairs experience is preferred.
Experience in working in teams with either a direct or matrix manager.  With support, assesses preferred option for tough decisions.
Candidates have developing knowledge and understanding of pharmaceutical/biological product development and regulatory requirements for product development and approval in one key region (EU, US, Japan)
Experience working in Regulatory Affairs with agency interaction responsibility with at least 1 health authority is preferred.
Relevant experience working in a complex and matrix environment is preferred.  Ideal candidates will have clinical or device foundation.
 
Competencies:
 
Strong ethics and integrity
Developing ability to think strategically, assesses prudent risks and develop bold, agile, innovative approaches to complex challenges
Developing communication skills, with capacity to articulate complex concepts in a manner individuals at various levels in the organization can comprehend with support.
Support productive, working relationships within CSL (e.g. R&D and Commercial).
Fluency in English (verbal and written).

CSL Vifor is a global partner of choice for pharmaceuticals and innovative, leading therapies in iron deficiency and nephrology. We specialize in strategic global partnering, in-licensing and developing, manufacturing and marketing pharmaceutical products for precision healthcare, aiming to help patients around the world lead better, healthier lives. IQVIA™ – The Human Data Science Company™ – is a leading global provider of advanced analytics, technology solutions and clinical research services to the life sciences and healthcare industries. Our mission is to create intelligent connections that deliver unique innovations and actionable insights to help our clients improve healthcare outcomes worldwide.

We are currently looking for a talented and motivated Consultant to join the Primary Market Research Team within our Swiss Analytics & Advisory Services Team, based in Zürich and Rotkreuz, Switzerland.

This role combines qualitative primary market research in Switzerland with competitive intelligence. You will manage projects end to end, conduct and synthesize primary and secondary research, and translate complex market evidence into clear, actionable insights for pharmaceutical clients.
Working across dynamic specialty markets, you will partner directly with clients and healthcare experts to address key commercial questions and support informed decisions throughout the project lifecycle.

Main Responsibilities:

As a Consultant, you will manage multiple client projects simultaneously, collaborate with colleagues across a range of team structures, and serve as a key point of contact for clients.

Qualitative Market Research & Competitive Intelligence

Lead qualitative market research and competitive intelligence projects end to end for pharmaceutical clients across the DACH region
Translate client business questions into appropriate research approaches and structured project plans
Conduct primary research, including interviews with physicians and other healthcare professionals in German and, where appropriate, French
Complement primary research with targeted secondary research and desk analysis where required
Analyze and synthesize market, competitor, and stakeholder evidence to identify relevant insights, opportunities, and risks
Translate complex findings into clear, actionable commercial recommendations and compelling client storylines
Prepare high-quality reports and presentations and deliver results to client stakeholders
Own project timelines, deliverables, and day-to-day client interactions across the full project lifecycle
Manage several projects in parallel while collaborating effectively with colleagues across teams and disciplines
Contribute to the continuous development of research approaches, client solutions, and team capabilities

Qualifications, Experience and Skills

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree, ideally in life sciences or a related field
2–5 years of relevant professional experience in pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, healthcare consulting, market research, competitive intelligence, or a related field
Business-fluent German and English are required; conversational French is considered an asset
Knowledge and understanding of the Swiss pharmaceutical market
Strong analytical skills, with the ability to synthesize complex evidence into business-relevant insights
Excellent communication and presentation skills, with a confident and client-oriented approach
Effective project and time management skills, including the ability to prioritize and deliver high-quality work across parallel engagements
Structured and independent way of working, combined with a collaborative mindset and willingness to contribute across the organization

Reporting Line

The role reports to the Team Lead Qualitative Insights within the Primary Market Research Team of the Swiss Analytics & Advisory Services Team.

What We Offer

This role offers the opportunity to take genuine ownership of client projects, build trusted relationships with pharmaceutical stakeholders, and deepen your expertise across complex specialty markets. You will work at the forefront of healthcare innovation, supporting high-priority decisions around new and evolving therapies in areas shaped by scientific progress, significant investment, and active competition. With exposure to both qualitative market research and competitive intelligence, you will develop a broad perspective while contributing directly to decisions that can shape successful launches and market strategies.

IQVIA is a leading global provider of clinical research services, commercial insights and healthcare intelligence to the life sciences and healthcare industries. We create intelligent connections to accelerate the development and commercialization of innovative medical treatments to help improve patient outcomes and population health worldwide. Principal / Sr Principal, Health Economics, Health Technology Assessment
 
IQVIA™ is The Human Data Science Company™, focused on using data and science to help healthcare clients find better solutions for their patients. IQVIA offers a broad range of solutions that harness advances in healthcare information, technology, analytics and human ingenuity to drive healthcare forward. 

Job Overview

As a senior member of the DTAS (Data, technology and Advisory Services) team, you will work directly with life sciences clients as a trusted partner, helping them navigate complex strategic, technological, and operational challenges. You will shape and deliver high‑impact consulting engagements for senior stakeholders, building deep client intimacy through insight‑driven dialogue, proactive partnership, and consistent delivery excellence.

In DTAS we have Advisory Services clusters centered around accounts and specialist Centers of Excellence. The HE/HTA/V&A practice equips headquarter clients with best in class evidence and HTA strategy to secure pricing, reimbursement, and access, globally, regionally, and locally. Our team of experts drives innovation, offering development, business development and facilitates sharing of best practices and GTM materials for Health Economics (HE), Health Technology Assessment (HTA) and Value & Access (V&A) solutions.

Join our global HE/HTA/V&A specialist practice! We focus on creating global solutions that help clients design and execute evidence generation strategies, meeting payer and HTA requirements, and effectively communicating their product’s value story. You will be accountable for driving client satisfaction, identifying new opportunities, and achieving or exceeding assigned revenue targets.

Our integrated solutions are built on deep local knowledge of payers, global and local implementation capabilities, and unparalleled access to data. We excel in developing evidence generation strategies that maximize market access success, generating timely and cost-efficient evidence, and crafting compelling value stories for stakeholders. Our expertise spans health economics, statistics, evidence synthesis, systematic literature review, HTA, and real-world data. We believe in tailored solutions over templated approaches, requiring out-of-the-box thinkers to design the most suitable solutions for our clients.

This role will focus on expanding our HE/HTA business. It's a high-visibility opportunity to join a dynamic team, where the right candidate will find the pace and opportunities as energizing as we do!

Role Description
As a Principal within the HE/HTA/V&A Practice, your main focus is to deliver outstanding client service, while building trusted relationships with existing and new clients that enhance our brand and reputation in the business. Success will be measured by your ability to work directly with clients to develop business opportunities and deliver projects at high levels of client satisfaction.

Accountabilities
Acting as principal owner of all client engagements, i.e., from initial conversations to understand client needs, followed by the development of the right solutions to address these needs and overseeing project delivery
Creating and elevating new business opportunities through the identification of follow-on work as well as new opportunities with existing and new client organisations
Present educational and go-to-market materials about the offerings internally and externally
Identifying opportunities for selling our integrated solutions (projects including multiple offerings e.g. P&MA strategy, full HEOR/HTA support to prepare for P&R submissions, PRO instrument advice, RWE strategy)
Engaging closely with project teams in the design, development, and delivery of projects ensuring the full complement of IQVIA capabilities and solutions are utilised to address complex client issues
Establishing a culture of excellence and ensuring delivery of accurate and high-quality work which meets or exceeds client expectations
Fostering an environment of collaboration and inclusivity among project teams
Remaining current on industry, clients, and competitive trends and directions in order to anticipate and identify new business challenges and issues with assigned clients
Leading thought leadership and firm building initiatives that contribute to raising IQVIA's industry profile, e.g., through speaking engagements, client meetings, and publications
Mentoring, coaching, and sharing subject matter expertise with others to elevate our capabilities to deliver world-class solutions for clients
Leading ad hoc work streams on critical people-related issues such as recruitment, training and development
Serving as a development lead to 3-4 staff

Desired Qualifications, Skills, and Experience
Master’s Degree.
At least 10 years of professional experience in consulting, pharmaceutical, and healthcare industries with a focus on HTA or HEOR.
Experience with AI/ML is a plus.
Proven ability to build relationships, identify client pain points, and develop custom solutions targeted at HE/HTA  stakeholders.
A track record of driving HQ/global deals, aligned with suitable offerings development experience.
An established network of contacts in the pharmaceutical industry and payers.
A high degree of understanding of the processes underpinning payer evaluation and the factors and drivers impacting product development.
Deep commercial awareness of the healthcare, health technology, and pharmaceutical industries, gained through experience.
Demonstrated experience in market needs assessments and value proposition development.
Ability to express ideas clearly and concisely, tailoring messages to target audiences with the gravitas to build relationships and sell services.
Maintains a constant focus on industry, client, and competitive trends in the life sciences industry, applying this knowledge to both active client engagements and business/client development activities.
Applies an analytical approach to solving problems and reaching logical conclusions, gathering information from various sources and quickly understanding it. Works effectively with complicated, conflicting, or ambiguous information, identifying underlying patterns and causes.
Ability to speak clearly and fluently, demonstrating a logical, structured approach, adapting to the needs of the situation and audience, ensuring strong two-way communication.
Ability to write clearly and succinctly, adapting style and content to meet the demands of the situation and audience. Communicates clearly and effectively, using well-structured, logical arguments and avoiding unnecessary technical or complex language.
Considers the flow of money and resources through an organization, seeking to achieve commercial objectives such as profitability to ensure competitiveness and success.
Builds supportive relationships within a team, based on trust and respect. Listens to others, adapts to different work styles, and focuses on shared goals. Willing to challenge others and accept challenges to achieve the best results for the team.

When our values align, there's no limit to what we can achieve.
 
At Parexel, we all share the same goal - to improve the world's health. From clinical trials to regulatory, consulting, and market access, every clinical development solution we provide is underpinned by something special - a deep conviction in what we do.
Each of us, no matter what we do at Parexel, contributes to the development of a therapy that ultimately will benefit a patient. We take our work personally, we do it with empathy and we're committed to making a difference.

About Parexel
Parexel is a leading global clinical development partner delivering insights-driven clinical and consulting solutions to the life sciences industry. With 22,000+ employees worldwide, we partner with biopharmaceutical companies and research sites to design and deliver patient-focused clinical trials that broaden access and make research a care option for anyone, anywhere.

We work with focus, agility, and shared purpose, moving with urgency to address patient needs and accelerate the delivery of new therapies. We embrace bold thinking, adapt quickly to change, and continually raise the bar for the speed and quality of clinical research. We are expanding our team and seeking talented individuals to help drive industry-leading innovation, With Heart.

About the Role
We are seeking a Regulatory Affairs Consultant (Clinical Writing) to support global regulatory submissions and lifecycle activities across a diverse portfolio of pharmaceutical and biotechnology products. This is an opportunity to play a strategic role in bringing innovative therapies to patients by transforming complex clinical and scientific data into clear, compelling, and regulator-ready documentation.

Working within a collaborative, cross-functional environment, you will contribute to global development and regulatory strategies while partnering with Clinical, Safety, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Regulatory Affairs, and Regulatory Operations teams. Your expertise will directly support critical regulatory milestones and help advance programs throughout development, registration, and lifecycle management.

Key Responsibilities
Author clinical regulatory documents supporting global submissions and lifecycle activities, including CTD Module 2 Clinical Overviews and Clinical Summaries.
Develop integrated clinical documents supporting CTD Module 5, including Integrated Summaries of Safety (ISS) and Effectiveness/Efficacy (ISE), where applicable.
Prepare responses to Health Authority questions on clinical, epidemiological, and safety topics.
Create briefing packages for Regulatory Authority consultations, scientific advice procedures, and other Health Authority interactions.
Author and support Pediatric Investigation Plans (PIPs), Pediatric Study Plans (PSPs), Orphan Drug Designation applications, Diversity Action Plans, and other supporting regulatory documentation.
Define and plan clinical regulatory writing deliverables, including scope, content requirements, timelines, dependencies, contributors, and review strategies.
Interpret, integrate, and summarize complex clinical, safety, epidemiological, and statistical information into scientifically accurate, regulator-ready documents.
Contribute to regulatory strategy and planning activities supporting global clinical development, submissions, and lifecycle management.
Collaborate with Global and Regional Regulatory Affairs Clinical Leads to translate regulatory strategy into effective clinical content and documentation plans.
Lead and coordinate cross-functional authoring and review activities with subject matter experts across Clinical, Regulatory Affairs, Safety/Pharmacovigilance, Biostatistics, and Epidemiology.
Support the planning and delivery of marketing applications, post-approval supplements, variations, and other regulatory submissions.
Ensure all documents are scientifically robust, accurate, compliant, consistent, and submission-ready within agreed timelines.

Candidate Profile
You’ll thrive in this role if you bring:
Expertise in clinical regulatory writing, scientific communication, and regulatory submission development.
Strong experience interpreting and communicating complex clinical, safety, epidemiological, and statistical information.
A collaborative approach and the ability to work effectively across global, cross-functional teams.
Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, stakeholders, and timelines.
A commitment to quality, scientific accuracy, and regulatory compliance.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with a high standard of scientific and regulatory writing.

Required Qualifications
University degree in a scientific, medical, pharmacy, or related life sciences discipline.
At least 5+ years of relevant clinical regulatory writing and/or biopharmaceutical regulatory experience.
Demonstrated experience authoring clinical regulatory documents for global submissions, including CTD Module 2 clinical documents and integrated clinical documents such as ISS and ISE, where applicable.
Experience supporting INDs, CTAs, NDAs, BLAs, MAAs, and associated amendments, supplements, variations, and lifecycle submissions.
Strong understanding of the drug development process and the role of clinical evidence throughout development, registration, and lifecycle management.
Strong working knowledge of ICH guidelines and applicable global regulatory requirements and Health Authority expectations for clinical regulatory documentation.
Demonstrated ability to coordinate document development through authoring, review, approval, and finalization with cross-functional stakeholders.
Strong communication, organizational, project management, and problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications
Advanced degree in a scientific, medical, pharmacy, or related life sciences discipline.
Experience supporting global regulatory submissions across multiple regions and Health Authorities.
Experience contributing to regulatory strategy, lifecycle management activities, and Health Authority interactions.
Familiarity with regulatory submission planning, review management, and document finalization processes.

Benefits and Compensation
Health, Vision & Dental Insurance
Vacation/Holiday/Sick Time
Flexible benefit portal

If this job doesn’t sound like the next step in your career, but perhaps you know of someone who’d be a perfect fit, send them the link to apply!
We believe in flexibility, growth, and creating space for people to do their best work. Join us and be part of a team where your contributions help shape the future of clinical research.

The Senior Director, Global Clinical Development, Neuroscience will own the clinical strategy for one or more neuropsychiatry programs. Extensive experience in clinical development in neuropsychiatric indications is a requirement. Experience in formulation development in neuropsychiatry is a plus.
The Neuroscience Clinical Development function is part of a global scientific organization dedicated to initial evaluations of new molecules, biomarkers, and mechanistic hypotheses in humans. Ensure studies are designed to meet Regulatory, Quality, medical, and access goals

Medical Monitoring

Developing and implementing the clinical development strategy

Serving as principal functional author for Regulatory submissions, Clinical Study Reports, and scientific publications

Accountable for clinical contributions to clinical study reports (CSRs), regulatory reports, briefing books and submission documents

External Partnerships, Alliances, and Publications

Sits in team responsible for establishing key alliances with academic centers, co-operative groups, vendors and government agencies
Represents department in business development due diligence and partner alliance management as appropriate; sits on JDC/JRC/JSC as appropriate

Champions a quality-focused mindset and ensures adherence to GCP and compliance obligations for clinical conduct

MD or MD/PhD and deep clinical development expertise in psychiatry

7+ years of relevant experience in translational and/or clinical research in an industry or biotech setting
Extensive experience in clinical trial design and execution, and development strategy in pharmaceutical industry or biotech
Deep understanding of pharmaceutical discovery, development and commercialization
Track record of mentorship and/or management and/or matrix leadership

Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills to influence decision-making at all levels of the organization

Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills appropriately flexing based on audience; expertly leverages effective communication and negotiation skills to influence decisions
Experience in Hematology and/or Autoimmune Diseases preferred
Expected travel is 30% - globally

The Director, Clinical Science – Oncology Clinical Development GYN provides scientific leadership across defined components of study design, conduct, data review, and interpretation within an assigned clinical programme. The Director, Clinical Science partners closely with the Senior Scientist and cross-functional teams to support delivery of clinical studies, ensuring scientific quality, data integrity, and robust interpretation of clinical data. This role contributes to both study-level activities and broader programme insights, without holding accountability for asset-level strategy or overall study delivery.

This is a scientific individual contributor role requiring deep oncology clinical development expertise, strong analytical and collaboration skills, and the ability to operate effectively within a complex, matrixed environment.

Director, Global Real-World Evidence & Health Outcomes Scientist, Oncology
 
For drugs to be successful, there must be robust health outcomes data to support launch optimization, reimbursement and maintain market positioning.  Specifically, evidence must be generated and maintained throughout the product lifecycle as the standard of care changes, new competitors are introduced, and patents expire on existing competitors. The landscape is evolving quickly as trials demonstrating efficacy in an area of unmet need may receive expedited review, or orphan product status designation which affects both GSK and competitors launch timelines and approval requirements. More of our customers are developing sophisticated internal health outcomes capabilities and access to real world data that can be used to better understand unmet needs and real-world effectiveness of our medicines. We need to better understand how our customers define value and to effectively collaborate with them to ensure we are generating value evidence data that includes real world evidence and cost effectiveness analyses that are impactful for payers, health systems, providers, and patients.
 
The role of Director, Global Real-World Evidence & Health Outcomes Research Scientist, Oncology is critical to achieving this ambition by supporting asset teams to ensure that each medicine GSK brings to market is supported by scientifically credible, high quality, evidence that drives competitiveness and strong evidence-based product positioning, value propositions and value-based pricing.  The role is critical to support the alignment of evidence with evidentiary requirements of customers responsible for marketing authorization, recommendation and reimbursement leading to successful patient access, product use and commercial success.
 
This role will provide YOU the opportunity to lead key activities to progress YOUR career.  These responsibilities include some of the following:
 
Plan, design and execute multiple studies for a given asset and manage timelines, deliverables, and budget.
Assure quality of deliverables, including review and sign off project specifications, protocols, data analysis plans, final study reports, abstracts, posters and manuscripts, in adherence to SOPs.
Identify resources, references and analyses to inform scientific design and advise internal experts (medical affairs, clinical, commercial/market access) and external experts as needed in support of the asset team.
Translate needs for evidence into study concepts in alignment with strategic objectives and vision for the asset, e.g. development of study protocols and proposing innovative and cost-effective ways of developing and executing studies.
Develop and maintain a good working knowledge of real-world data resources, existing partnerships and public initiatives and become the point person for select sources to advise on their suitability to address given research questions.
Develop a deep understanding of customers’ needs, including clinicians and HTA requirements, and their acceptance of different types of evidence and impact of that evidence to their decision making.
Collaborate with internal teams and participate in best practice sharing sessions across the non-interventional study organization.
Build strong working relationships with stakeholder groups across medical, market access, R&D and commercial to ensure strategic alignment and optimal cross-functional collaboration and communication. 
Ensure key stakeholders, including TA aligned business leaders, are regularly updated on plans through periodic reporting.
Develop excellent working relationships with external thought leaders to ensure appropriate methods and research agendas are applied, in accordance with GSK policies.

Basic Qualifications:

MSc, or equivalent in health outcomes, health economics, epidemiology, pharmacy, health or life sciences.
3+ years of experience working in the pharmaceutical industry, preferably in a multi-national company.
Experience in Oncology or Hematology
Experience in planning and delivering individual projects, managing budgets and working within a matrix setting.
A history of designing a variety of RWE (Real World Evidence) studies including prospective observational studies, cross-sectional and retrospective cohort studies, chart reviews, and database analyses.
Experience in utilizing evidence for the development of HTA submissions, reimbursement and/or medical engagements.

Job Purpose:
The Director, Oncology Translational Medicine, Clinical Biomarkers is responsible for the development and effective implementation of biomarker and translational medicine strategies to support the clinical development of late-stage oncology assets.
As a key member of a Clinical Matrix Team (CMT), the Clinical Biomarker Director will collaborate with the Clinical Biomarker Executive Director to establish clear decision-making criteria, define patient segmentation strategies, and integrate these into clinical development plans.
You will leverage cutting-edge technologies and methodologies to discover and clinically validate biomarkers, ensuring the biomarker strategy is fully aligned with the clinical plan. This integration will optimise decision-making in drug development and enable the identification of the right patient populations for our medicines.
Key responsibilities:
Collaborating closely with the Clinical Biomarker Executive Director to drive the design, alignment, and execution of clinical biomarker and translational medicine strategies focused on identifying predictive biomarkers that enable clinical success.
Validating and implementing biomarker strategies, including target engagement, pharmacodynamic, and proof-of-mechanism biomarkers, for clinical-phase programs to support patient stratification, dose selection, and enable clinical go/no-go decisions.
Participating in tumor-specific Biomarker Matrix teams, with responsibility for executing clinical biomarker strategies for late-stage oncology programs, while working closely with internal and external stakeholders, as well as disease area strategy teams.
Representing Translational Medicine at Clinical Development Matrix Teams (CMT) to establish biomarker-driven decision-making criteria and their seamless integration into clinical study designs, aligning with clinical study objectives
Supporting disease area strategies and translational objectives by defining biomarker priorities, areas of interest, and generating decision-enabling evidence packages informed by real-world datasets, internal and external data and partnerships (For e.g., research collaborations, KEE consultations).
Identifying cutting-edge science and technological advances to incorporate into biomarker strategies for guiding indication selection, patient enrichment, and combination strategies.
Overseeing and/or developing sample testing plans and delivering high-quality biomarker data packages to inform clinical development and regulatory strategies.
Managing effective relationships with clinical and scientific operations, diagnostics, medical science, medical affairs, regulatory, portfolio management, and commercial functions.
Supporting the expansion of mechanism and disease understanding to generate insights for indication expansion and scientific exchange as needed.
Defining and studying mechanisms of resistance to enable reverse translation, inform next-line strategies, support patient enrichment, and influence life cycle management of assets.
Contributing to the company’s scientific credibility through publications and presentations.

The Medical Director, Oncology Clinical Development - GI is the physician within the clinical programme team, bringing medical expertise, clinical judgement, and a patient-centred perspective to the design, conduct, and interpretation of clinical studies. This role is accountable for medical monitoring and safety oversight, ensuring that patient safety and clinical integrity are maintained throughout study execution.

Operating within the clinical strategy defined by the Clinical Development Lead (CDL), the Medical Director partners closely with the Senior Scientist and cross-functional teams to ensure that the physician perspective is fully integrated into study delivery. The role serves as a core member of the Clinical Matrix Team (CMT), contributing to study-level decisions, investigator engagement, and regulatory interactions.

For more complex or multi-study programmes, the Medical Director may provide medical guidance to other physicians within the programme and contribute to broader clinical discussions that inform programme-level decisions led by the CDL.

In This Role You Will:
•    Serve as the physician within the clinical programme team, providing medical expertise across study design, conduct, safety oversight, and data interpretation
•    Lead medical monitoring activities for clinical studies, ensuring patient safety, clinical integrity, and compliance with the protocol and regulatory requirements
•    Interpret clinical and safety data from a physician perspective, generating insights that inform study-level and programme-level decisions led by the CDL
•    Partner with the Senior Scientist and cross-functional teams to ensure medical considerations are integrated into study execution and delivery
•    Contribute medical expertise to protocol development, ensuring clinical relevance, patient safety, and feasibility within the framework defined by the CDL
•    Serve as a core member of the Clinical Matrix Team (CMT), providing the medical voice in study-level discussions and cross-functional decision-making
•    Engage with investigators and Key External Experts (KEEs) to support study conduct, scientific exchange, and external representation of the programme
•    Contribute to regulatory documents, Health Authority interactions, and scientific communications from a physician perspective

Detailed Responsibilities:
Medical Monitoring and Safety Oversight
•    Lead medical monitoring activities for assigned clinical studies, including real-time clinical decision-making on patient eligibility, protocol-related medical queries, and safety oversight
•    Conduct and oversee medical review of clinical trial data, both directly and through oversight of delegated medical review activities
•    Interpret and contextualise safety data in collaboration with pharmacovigilance, ensuring appropriate signal detection, escalation, and benefit–risk assessment at the study level
•    Participate in safety review forums, including Safety Review Team (SRT) discussions, Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) data reviews, and internal governance as required
•    Ensure medical monitoring activities are conducted in compliance with GCP, ICH guidelines, and applicable regulatory frameworks

Study Design and Execution
•    Provide medical input into protocol development, ensuring clinical relevance, patient safety, and operational feasibility within the clinical strategy defined by the CDL
•    Apply clinical judgement to support protocol implementation, addressing medical questions that arise during study conduct and ensuring consistency with the study’s scientific objectives
•    Partner with the Senior Scientist to ensure that medical considerations are fully integrated into study execution, data generation, and operational delivery
•    Contribute to the development and review of key study documents, including the Informed Consent Form (ICF), protocol deviation management plan (PDMP), and study reference manual (SRM)
•    Provide medical input into clinical data generation activities, ensuring alignment with study objectives, patient safety considerations, and the Clinical Development Plan (CDP)

Data Interpretation and Scientific Contribution
•    Interpret clinical data from a physician perspective, translating findings into insights on safety, efficacy, and patient impact that inform decision-making by the CDL
•    Contribute to study-level and programme-level data interpretation, supporting the CDL’s assessment of benefit–risk and clinical positioning
•    Contribute to the development of scientific communications, including study reports, clinical study summaries, publications, and congress materials
•    Collaborate with investigators on the evaluation and development of abstracts, posters, and manuscripts derived from clinical programme data
•    Maintain current knowledge of the asset’s biological mechanism, disease landscape, evolving treatment paradigms, and competitive environment to inform clinical interpretation

Regulatory and External Engagement
•    Contribute medical expertise to regulatory documents and Health Authority interactions, including responses to clinical and safety queries
•    Support preparation of materials for regulatory submissions, advisory boards, and external engagements, providing the physician perspective on clinical data and safety
•    Engage with Key External Experts (KEEs), investigators, and scientific collaborators to support study conduct, scientific exchange, and relationship development
•    Represent the medical perspective at cross-departmental interactions, including Integrated Evidence Team (IET) and Medical Affairs strategy discussions, as delegated by the CDL
•    Contribute to the clinical and technical diligence assessment of business development opportunities as requested

Cross-Functional Collaboration and Clinical Matrix Team
•    Serve as a core member of the Clinical Matrix Team (CMT), providing medical leadership within study execution
•    Contribute medical expertise to disease area strategy, integrated evidence planning, and Medical Affairs discussions as appropriate
•    Collaborate across functions — including Clinical Operations, Biostatistics, Regulatory, and Pharmacovigilance — to ensure alignment on study objectives, patient safety, and data quality
•    Contribute to Oncology Clinical Development-wide initiatives and workstreams

The Medical Director, Oncology Clinical Development is the physician within the clinical program team, bringing medical expertise, clinical judgement, and a patient-centered perspective to the design, conduct, and interpretation of clinical studies. This role is accountable for medical monitoring and safety oversight, ensuring that patient safety and clinical integrity are maintained throughout study execution.

The role serves as a core member of the Clinical Matrix Team (CMT), contributing to study-level decisions, investigator engagement, and regulatory interactions.

For more complex or multi-study programs, the Medical Director may provide medical guidance to other physicians within the program and contribute to broader clinical discussions that inform program-level decisions led by the CDL.

Bringing innovative therapies to patients requires more than strong science. It demands regulatory strategies that navigate complex global requirements while maintaining a clear focus on patient needs. As Associate Director, Regional Regulatory Strategist, you will play a key role in shaping and executing regulatory strategies for CSL's development and commercial products, serving as the regional regulatory expert within Global Regulatory Strategy. Working closely with Global Regulatory Leads and cross-functional colleagues, you will help drive successful regulatory outcomes across major health authorities while contributing to a unified global regulatory voice.

This role sits at the intersection of science, regulatory strategy, and the business . You will help guide products through critical regulatory milestones, influence development plans, and engage with EU health authorities to support timely patient access to innovative therapies. By combining regional regulatory expertise with commercial and development insights, you will play an important role in helping CSL deliver medicines to patients while navigating an increasingly complex global regulatory environment.

As a key member of the Global Regulatory Strategy organisation, you will provide strategic regulatory leadership across development and marketed products, partnering with global and regional stakeholders to develop effective regional regulatory pathways and achieve positive health authority outcomes.

Partner closely with Global Regulatory Leads and cross-functional regulatory colleagues to develop and execute integrated global regulatory strategies.

Build strong partnerships across Regulatory Affairs, Development, and Commercial functions while supporting a collaborative, high-performing regulatory environment.

Experience engaging directly with health authorities and managing regulatory interactions for development or marketed products.
Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional teams and drive outcomes within complex matrix organisations.
Advanced communication, stakeholder management, and strategic thinking skills, with the ability to balance scientific, regulatory, and commercial considerations.

Provide scientific leadership across nephrology, rare kidney diseases and Patient Blood Management, including areas such as coagulation and iron.

An MD, PhD, PharmD or equivalent advanced scientific qualification.
3–5+ years of relevant experience within Medical Affairs, Medical Science Liaison, Clinical Research or a related pharmaceutical industry role.

Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional partners, including Commercial, Market Access, Regulatory and Clinical Development.

The opportunity to contribute to Medical Affairs strategies that can make a tangible difference for patients.
A highly scientific role combining external engagement, evidence generation and strategic Medical Affairs work.
The opportunity to collaborate with leading scientific experts and multidisciplinary teams in an international environment.

Opportunities for professional development and continued growth within an international organization.
A collaborative, purpose-driven working environment focused on science, innovation and patient impact.

The activity involves the development of the most appropriate cable testing techniques to perform quality control on cables procured for CERN, and establish aging requirements on cables operating in the CERN accelerators environment.
QARE service needs to perform and develop electrical tests for low-voltage cables, including insulation resistance, dielectric spectroscopy, and voltage-withstand testing. You will contribute to cable qualification, condition assessment, and quality control.

Perform electrical tests on radiation-resistant cables and insulation materials.
Prepare samples, test setups and measuring equipment.
Develop and validate test procedures and acceptance criteria for radiation-resistant cables.
Analyse the effects of ageing, temperature, humidity and radiation.
Process measurement data and identify abnormal behaviour.
Ensure calibration, traceability and safe operation of test equipment.
Write test procedures, technical notes and qualification reports.
Present results and recommendations to technical teams.

Experience with electrical measurements or laboratory testing.
Knowledge of resistance, capacitance, impedance, leakage current, and dielectric breakdown.
Familiarity with insulation testers, high-voltage equipment, LCR meters, or impedance analysers.
Experience analysing data using Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW, or similar tools.
Ability to write clear procedures and technical reports.
A careful, analytical and safety-conscious approach.
Knowledge of cable testing techniques, dielectric materials, measurement uncertainty, and relevant IEC/EN standards would be an advantage.

Quality control, cable qualification, and acceptance criteria.
Laboratory instrumentation and data acquisition.
Python for data processing, analysis, and visualisation.

Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.

Experience designing experiments, evaluating model outputs and comparing technical approaches.
Experience developing Python applications and integrating APIs or external services.
Experience deploying AI applications or integrating them into production systems.

Strong Python programming and software engineering skills, including API development, testing and integration.
Hands-on experience with AI/ML frameworks and modern AI technologies, such as LLMs, embeddings, RAG and agentic workflows.
Ability to design, develop and evaluate AI solutions, including benchmarking, quality assessment and performance optimisation.
Experience integrating AI models and services into existing applications.
Knowledge of containerisation (Docker), deployment practices and CI/CD workflows.
Familiarity with MCP, model serving, Kubernetes or cloud infrastructure would be an asset.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently, investigate emerging technologies and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams.
Spoken and written English, with a commitment to learn French.

a Master's degree with 2 to 6 years of post-graduation professional experience;
or a PhD with no more than 3 years of post-graduation professional experience.

EDUCATION AND DESIRED EXPERIENCE

Professional-level English, written and spoken

Job Description SummaryLocation: Basel, Switzerland (#LI-Hybrid)

This role will serve as the strategic workforce partner to Regulatory Affairs (RA), supporting a global organization of approximately 2,000 employees through a significant transformation agenda. The role will combine external insights, workforce data and predictive analytics, business acumen, and deep transformation expertise to shape the future workforce, capabilities, and talent strategy for RA, with particular focus on AI-enabled changes to workflows, skills, and ways of working.

 
Job Description
Key Responsibilities

Partner with the Global Head of Regulatory Affairs and RA Leadership Team to shape and influence the workforce and people agenda for a global organization of approximately 2,000 employees.
Translate RA’s complex business transformation agenda into a clear workforce strategy and execution roadmap, ensuring transformation priorities are operationalized effectively.
Anticipate the impact of AI, emerging technologies, new platforms, and evolving regulatory models on workflows, roles, skills, and future workforce requirements.
Define and build the future capabilities and talent strategy required for RA, identifying critical skills, capability gaps, and actions needed to prepare the organization for the future.
Bring strong external insights, workforce data, predictive analytics, and market intelligence to challenge existing thinking and influence strategic business and workforce decisions.
Lead the people and workforce dimensions of complex transformation, coaching and constructively challenging senior leaders while building alignment and bringing the organization through change.
Establish the workforce strategy role as a credible and high-impact strategic partner within RA, demonstrating tangible business value through deep understanding of the function and its operating environment.
Contribute as a member of the Development P&O Leadership Team, jointly shaping and driving the broader Development P&O strategy while ensuring strong connection between functional and enterprise priorities.

Essential Requirements

Significant experience in HR leading complex, large-scale business and workforce transformation, ideally within a global, highly matrixed organization.
Strong expertise in workforce strategy, strategic workforce planning, future capabilities, skills, and talent strategy, with the ability to translate business transformation into actionable workforce priorities.
Strong external orientation, with demonstrated ability to bring market trends, emerging practices, technology developments, and external perspectives into senior-level business discussions.
Highly data- and insight-driven, with experience leveraging workforce data, analytics, and ideally predictive insights to identify trends, challenge assumptions, and influence strategic decisions.
Exceptional senior stakeholder influencing and coaching skills, with the credibility and confidence to challenge senior leaders constructively, build alignment, and lead through ambiguity and change.
Strong business acumen and impact orientation, with a leadership style combining strategic thinking, grounded credibility, empathy, and a deep understanding of how organizations and functions operate.

Desirable Requirements

Experience shaping workforce implications of AI, automation, digital transformation, or technology-enabled operating model change, particularly around future skills, capabilities, and ways of working.
Experience within pharmaceuticals, life sciences, Regulatory Affairs, R&D/Development, or another highly regulated global environment.
